gaps.name: perf-segments-item-span-first
gaps.title: An event query by item skips segments that do not hold the item before testing their types
gaps.definition:
Problem: every API answer waits for state.snapshot (1.25-1.6 s on the factory record on an idle thread, 5-15 s under load). A profile on a copy of the factory's state puts 2.5 of 3.5 s in state.explain -> counted -> spec/items.py moved -> _late (spec/items.py:220), which refolds about 1,750 items per snapshot. Each refold is a Segments.query(item=...), and Segments._rows (ergostat/segments.py:436) runs the _types_matcher lambda (segments.py:131-137, 2.1M calls a snapshot) on every segment before it checks s.span(item), which rules out almost every segment.
Change: in _rows check the time and seq ranges, then s.span(item) when an item is given, and only then the types. Optionally cache each segment's matching type list per matcher.
Definition of done:
1. _rows returns the same rows for every argument combination and returns early when the item is not in the segment.
2. A unit test over a record with several sealed segments: a query by item, with and without skip/type, returns exactly the old answer for 50 random items; a counting matcher shows segments without the item are not type-tested.
3. The PR states the snapshot time before and after on a copy of the factory state (ERGOSTAT_HOME pointed at a copy); expected about 1.25 s to 0.8 s.
Files: ergostat/segments.py, its test under tests/.
Acceptance tests: the new unit test; the existing segment and store conformance tests unchanged; a snapshot on a record of 30+ sealed segments at least 30% faster with identical output.
Budget: 20 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: eta-works-out-on-the-factory-record
gaps.title: The completion estimates are worked out on the factory's record: no KeyError, items that cannot move never run a simulation to the horizon, and a failure is said
gaps.owner_items: 17 (also 2: a failed simulation is cached and tried again every 30 s, eta_api.py:14, 78, each try costing seconds)
gaps.definition:
Problem: on the live factory the Items Timeline stacks every gap at now because it never gets estimates. ~/.ergostat/ergostat-factory-678f59af/run.log has 6,443 lines `eta: KeyError: 'how'` and no successful run. The failure is ergostat/numbers/etamodel.py:292 (`elif r['how'] == 'ack':`), reached for an open run (taken, not ended) on an item whose own events moved it on after the take. web/eta_api.py _work (83-95) swallows the exception and caches None (retried no sooner than EVERY = 30 s), and relations.js then silently draws precedence.cpm's unlevelled forward pass (103 of 112 gaps start now). With that line fixed a run still takes 8.5 s: eta._Run.go loops `while self.heap and self.open > 0`, and paused items (43 parked gaps), items waiting on them (55 in all), items at a block commanded off and kinds with no finished state never finish, so with arrivals every run goes to the 90-day horizon (synthetic: 60 items 200 runs in 0.1 s; one paused item gives 53 runs in 5.1 s and p50 None). tests/test_eta.py has no paused case.
Words: 'holding' is a goal's word only (docs/vocabulary.md). An item the simulation leaves out is 'not scheduled', never 'held'.
Change: (a) etamodel.py:292 reads `elif r['end'] is not None and r['how'] == 'ack':` and an open run counts as going. (b) etamodel.read marks an item unscheduled when it is in a paused state, when its precedence predecessors reach an unscheduled item, when every block that takes from its state is off, or when its kind has no finished state; such items are not counted in _Run.open, not entered, and returned as {unscheduled: true, why: 'paused in parked' | 'waits on gap/x, which is parked' | 'waits for B, switched off'} with p50/p90 None; kinds[k] gains unscheduled (a count) and its p50/p90 cover movable items only. (c) eta_api._work keeps {error: '<type>: <message>'} instead of None and merge passes eta_error and unscheduled/why through. (d) relations.js note: with no estimates it says 'the simulation is being worked out' or 'failed: <error>'.
Definition of done:
1. etamodel.read on a record with an open run on an item moved past its take by its own events returns and counts the run as going.
2. One paused item with arrivals on: 200 runs in under 1 s, kind p50 not None, unscheduled == 1.
3. An item waiting on a paused item, and an item only at off blocks, are unscheduled with a reason naming the cause.
4. A simulation that raises is said on the Timeline with its error.
5. The four backtest records' table in docs/roadmap/overnight/eta.md is rerun and unchanged.
6. SPEC §5a Completion estimates says such items are left out of the run and counted.
Files: ergostat/numbers/etamodel.py, ergostat/numbers/eta.py, ergostat/web/eta_api.py, ergostat/web/static/relations.js, tests/test_eta.py, docs/SPEC.md.
Acceptance tests: test_eta.py::test_an_open_run_on_an_item_moved_on_by_its_own_events, ::test_paused_item_does_not_hold_the_run, ::test_waiting_on_a_paused_item_is_unscheduled, ::test_off_block_items_unscheduled, ::test_a_failed_simulation_is_said. After deploy (GET only): :8798/api/items-graph?kinds=gap has eta.runs >= 20 and run.log gains no 'eta: KeyError'.
Budget: 110 net lines including tests.

gaps.name: forward-pass-levelled-by-block-capacity
gaps.title: Before the estimates, and at a moment travelled to, the Timeline's forward pass is levelled by each block's capacity, read from one shared function
gaps.definition:
Problem: ergostat/precedence.py's projection (cpm in build) is the critical path method with no resources. It is drawn on every first paint before the estimates exist, at every moment travelled to (SPEC §5a: estimates are of now only) and whenever they fail. In it every unblocked or queued item starts now: on the factory record 103 of 112 gaps, 'done in about 7.6h' for about 110 gaps of median 3.2 h each. This is the owner's 'as if 100 gap runs start at once'. Capacity is read today only inside etamodel.read, which fails on the factory record until eta-works-out-on-the-factory-record lands (hence the dependency).
Change: (1) one function etamodel.capacities(project, snapshot) -> {block: {lanes, source}} is the only place a block's simulated capacity is decided (pool, or pool now from its stock, the agent's at-once, the daemon's concurrency, whichever binds), worked out once per snapshot and kept with it (never per request); eta.py and precedence.py both call it. eta-refused-takes-are-a-closed-gate later makes this one function return the measured concurrency, so the levelled pass and the simulation change together. (2) a deterministic levelled schedule in precedence.py, the serial schedule-generation scheme of resource-constrained scheduling: in precedence order, least slack first then longest path ahead (the dispatcher's tie-break), each item is placed at the earliest time its predecessors are done and the block that takes it from its state has a free lane; durations are the kinds' medians as now. (3) the projected bars, out['end'] and the legend's 'done in about' come from the levelled schedule. The unlevelled chain is still marked but is labelled for what it is: 'longest chain of waits, ignoring capacity'; the finish drawn and said is the levelled end, so the two never read as one claim (this amends filed Q60's 'agrees with the critical path': its clock time is the levelled, later the simulated, finish). (4) every time printed by the Timeline uses filed Q34's formatter (date and zone when not today). The legend says 'levelled by each block's capacity, median times; the simulation replaces it when worked out'.
Definition of done:
1. 100 unblocked items on a block of capacity 6 with a median of 20 min end at about 100/6 x 20 min, not 20 min.
2. No block has more lanes busy than its capacity in the levelled bars; dependencies are respected.
3. A moment travelled to shows levelled bars.
4. The levelling costs under 50 ms on 600 items, with capacities read from the snapshot's kept table (no record read in precedence.build).
5. The marked chain's label contains 'ignoring capacity' and the legend's finish equals the last levelled bar's end.
6. SPEC §5a The critical path describes the levelled projection and the label.
Files: ergostat/numbers/etamodel.py (capacities), ergostat/numbers/eta.py (calls it), ergostat/precedence.py, ergostat/web/static/relations.js, tests/test_precedence.py, tests/test_items_page.py, docs/SPEC.md.
Acceptance tests: test_precedence.py::test_forward_pass_levelled_by_capacity, ::test_levelled_respects_dependencies, ::test_capacity_comes_from_one_function; test_items_page.py::test_timeline_first_paint_is_levelled (on the roadmap fixture before estimates arrive no more than the developer block's 2 bars overlap).
Budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: timeline-shows-the-simulated-schedule-in-order
gaps.title: Timeline: rows in projected order, items not scheduled set apart with reasons, each block's capacity named
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner asks 'what finishes when and in what order'. Even with estimates, relTimeline's el.draw (ergostat/web/static/relations.js:222) orders rows by `segments[0][1] ?? es ?? first`: an open item's segments start at its creation, so rows follow creation order and the ranked backlog is scattered instead of a waterfall. Items the simulation leaves out (parked, or waiting on parked; the unscheduled flag from eta-works-out-on-the-factory-record) get no explanation, and nothing says which capacity the simulation used (the note at relations.js:362-366).
Change (no new page, panel or control): with estimates, unfinished rows are ordered by eta.start (p50), then eta.p50, then id; finished rows stay above as what happened. Unscheduled items go in a group at the end under 'Not scheduled (N)', each row showing its why ('parked', 'waits on gap/x, which is parked') and no bar ahead. The word 'held' is not used (it is a goal's word). The legend's per-kind sentence (filed Q60's form, times through filed Q34's formatter) adds the count: 'last of 40 gaps expected Tue 24 Nov 14:10, by Wed 09:00 at worst (9 in 10); 3 not scheduled'. The note names each block's simulated capacity and source: 'implementor 9 at once (pool stock.implementor-pool now), reviewer 6' (eta_api.merge passes capacity sources). Before the estimates are worked out the note says 'Working out the schedule: a simulation of N unfinished <kind> at each block's capacity' and any bars drawn from the forward pass are labelled as such. The item page's estimate line says 'not scheduled: <why>'. SPEC §5a Timeline row updated.
Definition of done:
1. Unfinished rows are in projected-start order: the projected bars' left edges are non-decreasing down the rows.
2. Unscheduled items are grouped last with reasons; no reader text on the Timeline contains 'held'.
3. The legend gives a clock time with its date and the count not scheduled.
4. The note names each block's capacity and source.
5. With the eta stubbed to None the note contains 'Working out the schedule'.
Files: ergostat/web/static/relations.js, ergostat/web/eta_api.py, ergostat/web/static/pages.js (item page line), docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_items_page.py.
Acceptance tests: browser on a fixture of 30 items with a 3-wide pool and ranks opposite to creation order (edges non-decreasing, at most 3 bars overlap at any x); a paused item and its dependent under 'Not scheduled (2)'; live check GET only on :8798/items?kind=gap&view=timeline: a staircase, not all at now. Rebase onto filed Q59/Q60 if they landed.
Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: eta-refused-takes-are-a-closed-gate
gaps.title: A block's refused takes are its gate closed, not runs: the estimates and the levelled pass take the concurrency the control loop allows
gaps.definition:
Problem: once the estimates run on the factory record they still schedule 36 implementors at once, because block implementor's pool reads 36 (run/pools.json); all 151 gaps start within 6 minutes, and the levelled forward pass reads the same 36. That is still the owner's complaint. The factory itself held stock.gaps-building at a mean of 6.1 over the last day (1 now, 97 ready): the implement-when gate binds, not the pool. The record's attempts also misread the gate: of the implementor's 2,144 attempts 1,463 are uncounted give-backs (nack, count: false, put off 300 s, shorter than 30 s: the run refusing on drain or machine-full); merge-queue 744 of 870. eta.attempt() replays each as a run that holds a seat and adds rework.
Change: (a) etamodel._leases leaves uncounted give-backs shorter than MIN_RUN (30 s) out of a block's attempts; they become the block's refusals (a share of takes refused, and their put-offs). (b) etamodel.capacities (the one function of forward-pass-levelled-by-block-capacity) caps each block's lanes at its measured effective concurrency: the p90 of runs going at once while items waited in its states, sampled from the leases' taken/ended intervals over HISTORY, never above its capacity, with source text ('6 at once while items waited (the record, p90), under its pool of 36'); the simulation and the levelled pass therefore change together. (c) tests/eta_synthetic.py gains a gated record (pool 20, a gate admitting 4 at once, refusals put off 300 s) and the backtest table its column; each of (a) and (b) is kept only if it lowers MAE or raises p90 coverage there without worsening the four existing records beyond their run-to-run spread; the table and verdict go in docs/roadmap/overnight/eta.md (this may reverse its dropped Little's-law cap).
Definition of done:
1. On the gated synthetic record neither the simulation nor the levelled pass ever has more than the measured concurrency at once.
2. The owner's picture: on a copy of the factory record (and on the gated synthetic record in CI) no more gaps start in the first projected hour than the implementor's measured concurrency, in both the first paint and the simulated Timeline.
3. The p50 MAE on the gated record falls by at least a third against the current model.
4. Each block's source text names its measured concurrency when it binds.
5. SPEC §5a says how refusals and measured concurrency enter.
Files: ergostat/numbers/etamodel.py, ergostat/numbers/eta.py, tests/eta_synthetic.py, tests/eta_backtest.py, tests/test_eta.py, tests/test_precedence.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/roadmap/overnight/eta.md.
Acceptance tests: test_eta.py::test_uncounted_refusals_are_not_runs, ::test_measured_concurrency_caps_a_gated_block, ::test_backtest_gated_record_improves; test_precedence.py::test_levelled_pass_uses_measured_concurrency.
Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: perf-web-requests-never-pile-up
gaps.title: The page server drops requests whose client left, bounds its queue, keeps a fast lane for cheap answers and logs each slow answer
gaps.definition:
Problem: on 2026-11-22 the live factory's page server (pid 9278, 165% CPU, 2.4 GB) stopped answering: /api/status gave nothing in 580 s and /static/style.css waited 228 s. It held 66-84 CLOSED and 5-10 CLOSE_WAIT sockets: requests whose clients had sent their GET and gone, still queued. PooledServer (ergostat/web/__init__.py:28-50) has 24 workers fed from one unbounded queue and runs every job however long it waited; static files wait in the same queue. run.log has about 195 'the client went away' lines (48 in an hour from /api/loop-control), each an answer built for nobody, and nothing records queue wait or work time. No page script aborts its fetches when the page is left.
Change: (1) detecting a client that left: a worker takes the job before the request is read, and a client that sent its GET and then closed still has its request bytes waiting, so a peek before reading returns those bytes, not b''. So the handler first reads and parses the request line and headers (as it does now), and only then, before calling _answer for a GET, checks the socket: select() says readable and recv(1, MSG_PEEK | MSG_DONTWAIT) returns b'' means the client sent FIN: drop the job and count it. (A pipelined second request gives bytes, not b'', and is served.) A GET that waited in the queue more than 60 s is dropped too. A POST that has been read is never dropped. macOS has no POLLRDHUP, so nothing relies on it. (2) the queue is bounded (256); past it new connections get 503 with Retry-After: 2. (3) static files, / and answers that need no snapshot go to a fast lane of 4 workers the API queue never fills. (4) every answer over 2 s writes one run.log line: 'web: slow GET /api/x: waited 4.1s in the queue, 3.0s working, 77 KB'; counts by path are kept in memory and carried by /api/status as `web` when any was slow in the last 10 minutes. (5) util.js apiText aborts a page's in-flight fetches (AbortController) when its page element leaves the document.
Definition of done:
1. A client that sends a complete GET and then closes before a worker is free (the measured CLOSE_WAIT case) is never handed to _answer.
2. With all API workers blocked, /static/style.css answers in under 200 ms and the 257th queued connection gets 503 at once.
3. A slow answer writes one line with queue wait and work time.
4. No read POST is ever dropped.
5. Leaving a page cancels its in-flight fetches.
Files: ergostat/web/__init__.py, ergostat/web/server.py (the check before _answer, timing in do_GET), ergostat/web/static/util.js, tests for the web server, one browser test.
Acceptance tests: a unit test that opens a socket, sends a full GET, shuts down its write side and closes while every worker is busy: _answer is not called for it (on macOS and Linux); 24 slow requests (5 s each) plus 30 whose clients send and hang up after 1 s: the server does the work of the 24 only and the log names them; unit tests for 2-4; a browser test for 5.
Budget: 140 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: perf-answers-never-wait-for-a-snapshot
gaps.title: Page answers use the last snapshot while the next is built, say how old it is, and never wait on the model-file check
gaps.definition:
Problem: Live.snapshot (ergostat/web/server.py:151-180) keeps the live snapshot 1.5 s but a build costs 1.3 s idle and 5-15 s against the engine, and _answer (server.py:417-446) builds or waits for one before dispatching any answer, including those that never read it (projects, guide, messages, actions, inbox, report). Pages poll every 2.5-5 s (diagram.js:1256, main.js:50), so nearly every poll pays for a rebuild: status 13.3 s, systems 5.6 s, the next request 2 ms. Live.get() (server.py:181) calls Settled.due() -> model.stamp (model.py:569-592), which re-parses all 25 YAML files every 10 s on whichever request comes first (0.5 s).
Change: (1) one background thread keeps the live snapshot per window in use, rebuilt when the last is done, at most every 2 s; a request takes the newest and never waits unless none exists; a snapshot older than 15 s makes requests wait as now; a past moment (at=) is unchanged; a model change is never served stale; a window nobody asked for in 60 s stops being refreshed. The thread exposes one hook, after_snapshot(fn, budget), that later gaps use for per-goal work (the performance word, the forecast) under one stated time budget, so no second worker thread is added to this process. (2) the snapshot is lazy in _answer: heads that do not read it do not build it. (3) the model-file check and reload run on the background thread every second; Live.get() only returns the current project. (4) each snapshot records snap['built_in'], and every answer carries snap['at'].
Definition of done:
1. With a snapshot builder that sleeps 2 s, ten concurrent status requests made 2 s after the first build all answer in under 0.2 s and one rebuild runs.
2. projects, guide, messages, actions and inbox do not call state.snapshot.
3. Live.get() never calls model.stamp on the calling thread, and a model edit is taken within 3 s.
4. No answer is older than 15 s, and its age is in the answer.
5. Work registered with after_snapshot runs on the one thread, stops at its budget and resumes after the next snapshot.
Files: ergostat/web/server.py (Live, _answer), ergostat/reload.py if the watcher needs a hook, tests for the web server.
Acceptance tests: unit tests for 1-3 and 5; on a copy of the factory state the p95 of status, loops, items?per_kind=25&shown=1 and graph?view=dynamics polled every 2.5 s for a minute is under 0.5 s (before/after p50 and p95 in the PR).
Budget: 140 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: perf-header-projects-list-is-cheap
gaps.title: The header's project list holds running projects only, worked out off the request path; the CLI's list is unchanged
gaps.definition:
Problem: every page load's header asks /api/projects (ergostat/web/static/util.js:356-395). projects.known (ergostat/projects.py:52-78) walks every folder under ~/.ergostat (2,534 on the owner's machine: 1,479 with the repository gone, 1,054 stopped, 1 running) and for each loads the model and takes a snapshot (_row, projects.py:33-49) under one global lock. On the live factory it took 113 s, then 32 s, for 349 KB, holding a worker and the GIL every other answer needs; cold it gave no answer in 120 s. The resulting select has 2,534 options, 2,533 disabled. projects.known is also what `ergostat projects` prints (ergostat/cli/running.py:348), so it must keep listing stopped projects.
Change: (1) projects.known stays as it is for the CLI. A new projects.running() lists only projects whose engine runs (running_pid, web.json), each with its goals-off counts, and a cheap count of the stopped ones (folders counted, no model loaded). (2) the page server works running() out on a background thread every 60 s; /api/projects reads the last list and takes no global lock; a stopped project's model is never loaded in the page server. (3) the header menu lists running projects, then one muted line 'N stopped (ergostat projects)'. Default, no owner question: the switcher drops stopped projects.
Definition of done:
1. With 2,000 fake folders (2 running) /api/projects answers in under 0.3 s, under 20 KB, and loads two models.
2. No model load or snapshot of another project happens inside a request.
3. The menu still switches to a running project and shows its 'N off'.
4. `ergostat projects` still lists stopped projects, with the same rows as before (a CLI test).
Files: ergostat/projects.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/static/util.js (refreshProjects), tests.
Acceptance tests: the 2,000-folder unit test (time, size, rows); the CLI test for 4; a browser check of the menu; on the owner's machine /api/projects under 0.5 s cold (GET only).
Budget: 90 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: perf-goals-page-asks-once
gaps.title: The Goals (Loops) page asks for all goals' performance in one answer and stops fetching the whole graph for sparklines
gaps.definition:
Problem: opening Loops on the factory sends one /api/loop-control?goal= per goal (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:45-51; also review.js:304): 60-97 at once. Each is an identification serialised by control_api.WORKING (ergostat/web/control_api.py:14-33), so they finish between 0.2 and 9.4 s, each holding one of the 24 workers; the header's status (4.8 s) and the next page's HTML (4.6 s for /items) wait behind them. Every 30 s the page also fetches graph?open=* (2.4 MB) only to draw each stock's sparkline (pages.js:30-36). Live.keep (ergostat/web/server.py:128-132) clears the whole answer cache above 16 entries, so the burst flushes its own results and the numbers, models and fit entries.
Change: (1) /api/loops?perf=1 carries each goal's performance word from one per-goal background cache (a small module, ergostat/web/goal_work.py: a table keyed (goal, what, window) with an age, filled goal by goal within a stated time budget; 5 minutes' life for the performance word); a goal not done says 'being worked out'. The cache is the one place per-goal background work is kept: forecast-on-first-paint-window-horizon adds its entries to it instead of starting a second worker. It runs on its own thread here and moves to the snapshot thread's after_snapshot hook when perf-answers-never-wait-for-a-snapshot has landed (whichever lands second does the two-line move). (2) the loops answer carries each goal's stock points (the snapshot holds them), so the page no longer asks for the graph. (3) Live.keep becomes an LRU of 256 entries. (4) the single loop-control for an opened goal's panel stays; review.js's fan-out reads the same summary. The row's columns are not redesigned here (goal-row-one-renderer does that on this answer).
Definition of done:
1. Opening the page sends at most 4 API requests (status, loops, projects, one more), none of them graph and none per goal (browser test on a demo).
2. The performance column fills within a few polls and matches loop-control per goal.
3. Unit test: of 40 cache entries the most recently used are kept; nothing younger than its lifetime is dropped under 256 entries.
4. The per-goal work never exceeds its budget per pass (unit test with a slow identification).
Files: ergostat/web/static/pages.js (pageLoops), ergostat/web/static/review.js, ergostat/web/server.py (loops, keep), new ergostat/web/goal_work.py, ergostat/web/control_api.py, tests.
Acceptance tests: the request-count browser test; the LRU unit test; on a copy of the factory state the page shows its table in under 3 s and a second tab loads /items HTML in under 0.5 s meanwhile. Note: keep internal names (pageLoops) so goals-page-replaces-loops-page applies either way.
Budget: 130 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: perf-factory-size-fixture
gaps.title: A script builds a factory-size state directory, so page speed and size can be tested without the live factory
gaps.definition:
Problem: every measurement of owner item 2 was taken by hand on a copy of the live factory's state, and the live server (:8798) answered no API GET within 60-580 s for any explorer. Several gaps need 'a factory-size fixture' for acceptance (page budgets, answer sizes, forecast refresh, the estimates' cost), and none exists: tests/fixtures holds no state directory, and diagram-large-case-fixture saves only /api/graph JSON. The live record cannot be shipped (it holds the owner's work).
Change: a script scripts/factory_fixture.py (using scripts/scale_model's generator where it fits) writes a model and a seeded record into a directory given on the command line, deterministic for a seed, of a stated size matching the factory's measured shape: about 25 model files, 60 goals in 8 systems (two of them made by `use: modelling`), 260 sensors, 37 machine blocks, 8 item kinds with 1,500 items (one kind of 430 with depends_on chains, 40 of them paused, 10 dead), 30 sealed segments of events over 24 h, about 2,000 lease attempts with 60% uncounted give-backs on one gated block, and one goal with a planted off stretch of 20 minutes and one upkeep goal off. A pytest fixture `factory_state` builds it once per session into tmp (skipped under a `-m fast` run) and can start a page server on it. docs/roadmap or tests/README says what it holds and that live-factory numbers in a PR are taken on a copy by hand, not in CI.
Definition of done:
1. `uv run python scripts/factory_fixture.py OUT --seed 1` writes a state directory that `ergostat check` passes and whose counts match the sizes above (asserted by a test).
2. Two runs with one seed give byte-identical records.
3. A snapshot on it costs within a factor of two of the factory copy's (the PR gives both numbers).
4. The pytest fixture serves /api/status and /api/items from it.
Files: new scripts/factory_fixture.py, tests/conftest.py (the fixture), tests/test_factory_fixture.py, a README line.
Acceptance tests: the counts test, the determinism test, the served-answers test.
Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: goal-state-says-its-system-and-upkeep
gaps.title: Each goal's state says its system and whether it is the modelling system's own, and one server function makes the goals-off counts
gaps.owner_items: Decision: the modelling system's goals come out of the headline (shown beside it)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the headline counts every goal with status off, computed in the browser (ergostat/web/static/util.js:364); the switcher counts off and open (ergostat/projects.py:44-48), a second definition. A goal's state in the snapshot (ergostat/state.py:304-312) carries neither its system nor whether a once template made it, so filed Q14 (headline), Q16 (rows by system), Q42 (side list groups) and Q13 would each invent a predicate. On :8791, :8792, :8796 and :8797 the red '2 loops off' is entirely modelling's requests-handled and model-fits (shots/plan-goalvocab-8791-loops.png, plan-goalvocab-8792-phone-home.png). The predicate exists: ergostat/spec/ir.py:336 once_made(spec, x). Precedent for setting goals apart: state.py:625-629 skips a remote's goals.

1. On every demo, in Dynamics and Blocks, top level, each system opened and everything open, no visible line is detached (over 6 px) at first draw, 100 ms after Wrap, Open all, Close all and Open of one system, and after routing.

gaps.name: diagram-drag-lines-follow
gaps.title: A dragged part's lines move with it in the same frame; a drop re-routes only what it touched
gaps.definition:
Problem (reproduced): on :8791 ?view=dynamics&open=* a fresh page's lines caught up 1.0 s into a drag; after one route() 7 lines were 103-184 px off, not greyed, 6 s later (shots/plan-dr-tf-drag-after-route-mid.png): the stale listeners of an earlier page took the shared S.nodeDrag (removed by the page guard of diagram-lines-stay-attached, which this builds on). What remains is the drag itself: each move is a whole libavoid transaction with crossing weighing (ergostat/web/static/avoid.js:283,292): 0.4-2 s. putDown (interact.js:165) calls avoidStart, a full re-route of every line (1.7 s on ticket-factory; never finishes on the factory). A stock dragged out of its open system's frame is left outside (layout rule 7). The existing drag tests (tests/test_diagram_rendering.py:556,614,672) drag only on a fresh page.
Change (uses standIn and the page guard of diagram-lines-stay-attached; adds no second stand-in and no second guard): (1) on every pointermove each line touching a moved part is redrawn with standIn from the parts' current places (its end on the part), greyed; lines not touching it are untouched. (2) drag moves route with crossingPenalty 0 (avoidCore move/moveMany, avoid.js:274-295); the careful weight is used on the drop's own lines. (3) a drop re-routes only the lines touching what moved (avoidMoveMany on the router state the drag built); a full routing only when none exists. (4) a part dropped outside its open system grows that system's outline; same in Blocks frames.
Definition of done:
1. After 0, 1 and 3 route() calls a 150 px drag updates only the visible SVG.
2. At every sample (each 100 ms) no drawn line end is more than 6 px from its part, in Dynamics, Blocks and Process.
3. Lines not touching the dragged parts keep their paths through drag and drop; touched lines are final within 1 s on every demo.
4. A part dragged out of its system's frame ends inside the grown frame.
Files: ergostat/web/static/interact.js, avoid.js, places.js (frame grows), tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: test_drag_after_route (toggle a system open and closed with S.toggleSystem, drag a stock 150 px, probe each .edge path's ends against its parts' boxes every 100 ms; untouched paths byte-equal; frame contains the part); the same in Blocks; existing drag tests pass.

gaps.name: items-kinds-say-which-states-finish
gaps.title: Each item kind says which of its states are finished, from one function for the Items page, the dependency graph and the estimates, and the page shows it
gaps.owner_items: 4 (which states are 'done'), 1 (the definition the default filter hides)
gaps.definition:

gaps.name: items-list-hides-finished-by-default
gaps.title: Items lists leave finished items out by default from one page-wide choice, never hide a searched or linked item, and a filter click answers at once
gaps.definition:
Problem: /items lists every state by default (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:642-644 asks per_kind=25 of all states), so finished work fills the lists: on the-job pr shows 3 open in 25 rows and mention 1 in 25 (shots/plan-items-8792-top.png); on the factory gap has 92 parked, 31 merged, 7 closed against 77 open. A filter click (go(), pages.js:614-622 -> replaceRoute, util.js:455 -> refresh()) is not a document load but re-asks items, each kind's items-flow (about 2.5 s each on the-job), the trust table and items-graph one system after another (await in a loop, pages.js:674-678) with nothing shown meanwhile, and the same /api/items went out three times in 7 s (click, then the 4 s poll twice): it looks like a reload that hangs (plan-items-8792-afterfilter.png).
Change: one finished choice for the whole Items page, one address parameter finished=hide|waits|show, read by the list, each kind's section, Graph and Timeline through one helper in pages.js (itemsFinished()); this gap adds hide and show, items-graph-one-show-choice adds waits (which the list treats as hide). The reader's word is 'unfinished' (never 'open', which already means an opened system and an open loop).
(a) server: GET /api/items takes finished=hide|show (default hide). Hidden = the kind's finished states from finish_of (spec/finished.py) plus dead; paused states (parked) stay; a lives-on kind hides nothing. Three things are never hidden, whatever the parameter: an explicit state= (state=closed shows closed); an item set carried by a link (a stock's, valve's or closed box's 'Show them on the Items page': the list shows exactly that set and its count equals the stock's or valve's count); and search matches (q=): a finished match is listed and counted apart ('1 finished match'). Counts per kind and state are unchanged; the answer adds per kind `hidden`. Paging uses the index's states list (spec/items.py _paged / in_states_page), not a filter after the cut.
(b) page: one toggle beside the search, 'Show finished', writes finished=show with replaceState; under each kind a note 'N finished (merged, closed, dead) not shown · show', whose link flips the same page-wide parameter (no per-kind finished control). Defaults, no owner question: dead letters are hidden and counted in the note; parked stays listed.
(c) a click shows 'Loading…' under the heading at once, a newer click aborts the older request (AbortController), the poll never overlaps a pending click, the per-system items-graph requests run in parallel (Promise.all), and a state click within a kind already loaded filters the loaded rows before the server answers. Snapshot mode applies the same filter client side.
Definition of done:
1. /items on a fixture lists no item in a finished or dead state, and each kind with any says how many are hidden and which states.
2. /items?finished=show lists them; the toggle and the note's link write and read the one parameter; no second finished control exists on the page.
3. /items?kind=gap&state=closed on a factory-shaped fixture lists closed gaps.
4. A parked gap is listed by default; dead is hidden and counted in the note.
5. Story F1: searching the id of a finished item finds it, with '1 finished match' said.
6. Story F4: following 'Show them on the Items page' from a stock that counts a finished state lists exactly as many items as the stock's value.
7. With the API delayed 2 s a state click shows 'Loading…' or filtered rows within 100 ms, and exactly one /api/items request follows it; no document load event fires after the first.
8. SPEC §5a documents the default, the parameter and the three exceptions.
Files: ergostat/web/server.py (items handler, _as_listed), ergostat/spec/items.py, ergostat/web/static/pages.js (pageItems default, toggle, itemsFinished, go/refresh), docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_item_sets.py, tests/test_items_page.py.
Acceptance tests: unit listing over gaps in merged, closed, parked, dead, open (default: open and parked; finished=show: all five; state=closed: one; q= of a merged id: found); the item-set count test; browser tests for the note, the parameter and points 5-7.
Budget: 170 net lines.

gaps.name: items-graph-one-show-choice
gaps.title: Graph and Timeline read the page's one finished choice, with a middle level 'and what they wait on', replacing Frontier and Collapse done
gaps.definition:
Problem: in Graph, Collapse done defaults on (pages.js:566) and removes every finished item with no unfinished child (relations.js:52); Frontier only decides whether those same items are in scope (relations.js:43), so toggling it changes nothing (reproduced on :8794: shots/plan-items-rm-graph-frontier1.png and -frontier0.png identical). With both off about 1,000 finished cards are drawn unreadably small (plan-items-rm-graph-f0c0.png). In Timeline, Frontier keeps every predecessor 'however far back', so on roadmap the whole history is still listed (plan-items-8794-timeline.png vs -timeline-nofrontier.png). Neither names what 'done' is.

Graph and Timeline read the page's one finished parameter through itemsFinished() (items-list-hides-finished-by-default owns it; that is the dependency), and the page's one control becomes a three-way segmented control 'Finished items: Hidden / Those waited on / Shown' writing finished=hide|waits|show. hide: unfinished and paused items only; a chain through finished items is one dashed line 'via N finished'. waits: plus finished items an unfinished one waits on directly (one hop). show: everything in the window. The list view treats waits as hide. Default hide everywhere; Timeline opens on waits unless the address says otherwise (a default, not a second control). Old frontier= and collapse= are read once and mapped. The legend says what is not drawn and why: '968 finished not drawn: gap merged, closed', from the answer's kinds[].finished (precedence.py:412). rgModel takes o.finished. The RG.NODES cap note stays for show.
Definition of done:
1. The two checkboxes are gone from both views; no 'Frontier', 'Collapse done' or 'Show: Open' text remains; the page has one finished control in all three views.
2. On the roadmap fixture the three options draw strictly increasing numbers of cards or rows.
3. waits never adds an item more than one precedence link from an unfinished one.
4. The legend names each kind's finished states and the count not drawn.
5. /items?view=graph&frontier=0&collapse=0 opens with Shown pressed; switching list -> Graph keeps the choice.
6. SPEC §5a table rows for Graph and Timeline updated.

gaps.name: valve-panel-lists-its-leased-items
gaps.title: A valve's panel lists the items its block has taken now, counts them right, and says how many wait
gaps.definition:
Problem: a valve's side panel says only 'BLOCK works items of kind K: N leased now. Show the leased items' (ergostat/web/static/itemsets.js:86-95 countsLines; used by dynamics.js:613 and details.js:108; server.py:778-780 from spec/item_sets.py:399-410 leased_by). And the count is wrong: on :8794 Dynamics, delivery, valve 'started' reads '0 leased now' while its own 'Items through it' table shows two rows 'leased by developer' and /api/items shows ticket/e203-release in state doing with lease.block developer (shots/plan-ks-road-valve-started.png, reproduced three times). Cause: leased_by builds ItemSet(states=[LEASED], where lease.block=B); once a run's first event moves the item out of 'leased' it is no longer counted though the block still has the lease. The owner wants those items on the valve's sidebar.
Words (docs/vocabulary.md, 'Items and leases'): an item a block has leased is 'taken' or 'being worked by <block>'; 'held' and 'holding' are a goal's words and are not used here.
Change: (1) a taken item is one whose lease has a holder, whatever its state; leased_by counts those per block and returns a set the Items page can open (a taken filter, shown exactly per items-list-hides-finished-by-default's item-set rule when that has landed), plus `waiting` (items of the kind in the block's takes.at states, not taken, matching its where) and `at`; the answer's fields are taken and waiting. (2) in countsLines, for each entry with taken > 0, fetch up to 10 of the set and draw a table under the line 'being worked by developer (3)': id (link to /item/ID), title (itemTitle), its state, run (first 8 chars, link to the Record), taken for, expires in ('overdue 1m' in the bad colour), attempt n of max; reuse leaseCells (pages.js:819) as one helper filed Q30 can use. More than 10: 'all N taken' links to the set. None: 'developer is working nothing now'. (3) the list is re-read every 4 s only while the panel is open and taken > 0; an unchanged answer leaves the DOM alone. Both the Dynamics and the Blocks/classic panels.
Definition of done:
1. leased_by counts items with a lease holder in any state; an acked one is not counted.
2. The valve panel lists each taken item with the facts above in Dynamics and Blocks.
3. A lease taken or ended while the panel is open appears or goes within 8 s without a reload.
4. The line says 'N waiting at STATE' or 'none waiting'.
5. No reader text in the panel contains 'held' or 'holds'.
6. .leases-line and its link remain (tests/test_items_page.py:328 passes unchanged); SPEC §9.5 names the list.

Acceptance tests: unit: an item taken then moved to a later state by its run is counted; browser: test_a_valves_panel_lists_each_taken_item (row link href /item/hypothesis%2F1, text contains the block), a lease taken/ended appears/goes, 'working nothing now' with 'waiting at'. Each fails on main.

gaps.name: item-page-fields-flow-and-lists-are-cards
gaps.title: An item's page lays short fields in a flowing grid, shows lists of records as cards with files behind disclosures, and keeps field history in one section
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner calls the item page very good, but short fields waste width, 'history (N changes)' sits on every field, and 'contexts' 'nests to the right, renders nested markdown in tables'. Cause found: contexts is a fold: append field of gap (ergostat.yaml:137); each entry is brief.assemble's dict (dev/bin/brief.py:85-88): a live gap (gap/queue-picks-mergeable) has 6 entries with 17 keys, one a list of about 20 ids, one `brief: file:run/briefs/...md`. fieldView (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:197-203) renders any list of objects as a table with a column per key and each cell recursively; a file: string goes to fileView (pages.js:186-194), so each whole Markdown brief is rendered inside cell 15 of 17, inside the td of table.fields. Depth only stops nested objects. refreshFiles (pages.js:228) re-asks every file each 4 s. 30 of that gap's 47 fields are short scalars on full-width rows, each with a details.history (pages.js:953); history is 43% of /api/items/ID (32.8 of 77 KB for ticket/SCRUM-2 on :8791), sent on every poll. Same smaller on :8792/item/review%2F2243 (shots/plan-ks-job-item-review.png).
Change (pageItem's Fields section only; other fieldView callers pass their mode and keep their output):
1. Short fields (number, boolean, string of 60 chars or fewer, not file:) go in a grid (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(11rem, 1fr))), name small and muted above the value; the kind's show: fields first, then by name.
2. Every other field is a full-width block below, headed by its name.
3. A list of objects is a list of cards, newest first, 3 shown and the rest under a closed 'N earlier' details. In a card scalar keys flow as 'key value · key value'; a list of short strings wraps as chips; a nested object is a dl; a file: value is a closed details named by key and size, fetched and rendered full width only when opened (refreshFiles skips closed ones); headings in rendered Markdown are demoted below the page's h2. A list whose entries share at most 6 scalar keys stays a table. No table inside a table; a file is never rendered in a table cell (in a cell it is a link).
4. The per-field disclosure goes; a field with more than one change shows 'N changes' beside its name, opening one collapsed 'Changes' section at the page's end filtered to that field.
5. /api/items/ID sends history only when asked (history=FIELD|all; the counts always); `ergostat item ID --history` unchanged. This gap owns the history default of the item answer; perf-answers-carry-only-what-is-drawn adds only since_seq on top of it.
Definition of done:
1. On an item whose append field holds dicts with a file: key, no table is inside a td of the fields section and no Markdown is rendered until its disclosure opens; opened, it is as wide as the content column; scrollWidth equals clientWidth.
2. At 1440 px a gap with 30 short fields takes at most 6 grid rows.
3. A closed file disclosure is never fetched.
4. No field row has a history disclosure; Changes lists a field's changes latest first, each linked to its event.
5. The poll's answer has no history key unless the section is open.
6. A session's messages, a remote item, Items list cells and the claim/decision/action views render as before; a snapshot's item page shows Changes or says it is not held.
7. SPEC §5a (docs/SPEC.md:1267) says where history is shown and the API default.
Files: ergostat/web/static/pages.js (pageItem, fieldView mode, historyView, refreshFiles), style.css, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/spec/items.py, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py (1021-1030 pins the old disclosure), tests/test_items_page.py.
Acceptance tests: test_a_list_of_records_is_cards_with_files_behind_disclosures (contexts of two dicts each with brief: file:b1.md and 8 keys; /file/b1.md requested only after the click), test_short_fields_flow_in_a_grid (20 numeric fields, at most 4 rows at 1440 px by bounding boxes), test_field_history_is_one_section. Each fails on main. Rebase onto filed Q53, Q54, Q82 if they landed.
Budget: 220 net lines.

gaps.name: system-box-control-panel-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: the closed system box as the control panel, in Dynamics and Blocks (docs/proposals/system-box-control-panel.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1): decision 1 says the control panel is the diagram with everything folded away, and SPEC §4 and the image-squeeze README promise each closed box shows its measures with value, setpoint, health and trend. What is drawn is a name, 'N feedback loops inside' and at best port names with bare numbers: on the-job the first screen is two empty boxes, on big seven identical ones while goals are off; in Blocks a closed system is 'Q_service 3x3' (shots/story-1-b1-home.png, story-1-b1-blocks.png, story-4-big-home.png, story-7-h1-blocks.png). The goal rows change the box's size, the layout's cost and the ports' order, and several things are now decided by the owner (goal, not loop; a Dashboard whose goals panel wants the same row; corner frames; bundles meeting a box), so the remaining pieces start with a decision. It depends on nothing and starts at once, in parallel with the owner's list.

2. The request and layout cost is measured.
3. It is checked against docs/DISCIPLINES.md (no sensors or controllers in Dynamics; Blocks monochrome).

gaps.name: forecast-sentence-in-words

gaps.name: one-phrase-for-how-far-off
gaps.title: Outside Blocks, how far a goal is from its bound is said in one phrase from one function
gaps.definition:
Problem (R11 piece 5): the same goal reads 'desired = 0: excess 37', 'setpoint ≤ 0 (off by 36)' and 'error −36' on three surfaces (shots/story-6-g1-home.png, infod-tf-loops.png, ixdb-job-sd-open.png). gaps.name: perf-compress-large-answers
gaps.title: Large JSON answers are gzip-compressed for browsers that accept it
gaps.definition:
Problem: no answer is compressed (ergostat/web/server.py _send, 807-830), and the tunnel (<the tunnel host>) and a phone carry every byte. On the factory the Diagram's first graph answer is 1.47 MB (gzips to about 50 KB), then 242 KB every 2.5 s; items-graph is 0.97 MB (4.5 MB on ticket-factory), graph?open=* 2.4 MB, projects 349 KB, status 77-131 KB every 5 s.
Change: in _send, when Accept-Encoding includes gzip and the body is over 16 KB of JSON or HTML, send it gzip-compressed (level 1) with Content-Encoding: gzip and Vary: Accept-Encoding. The two bodies are different representations, so they do not share one strong ETag: the gzip body's ETag is the identity body's with the suffix '-gz' inside the quotes, and If-None-Match is compared after stripping that suffix, so a 304 is answered for either form.
Definition of done:
1. A large answer asked with Accept-Encoding gzip comes back compressed, with an ETag ending in -gz, and decodes to the same JSON; without the header it comes back as now with the plain ETag.
2. A request carrying either ETag in If-None-Match for an unchanged answer gets a 304 with no body.
3. The PR gives bytes before and after for graph?view=dynamics and items-graph on a demo.
Files: ergostat/web/server.py, its test.
Acceptance tests: the unit tests for 1-2; graph?view=dynamics on :8796 at least 5x smaller on the wire with the answer time up by no more than 20 ms.
Budget: 35 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: flows-only-arranges-the-flows
gaps.title: Flows only lays out and draws the flows alone with the current engine, with its own pins and Re-arrange in the menu
gaps.definition:
Problem: Flows only is a CSS class (ergostat/web/static/diagram.js:1066-1068 'a class, not a re-layout: nothing moves'; style.css:550-553). The pipes keep the places the full diagram gave them, spread around auxiliaries now hidden: on image-squeeze system=lab the small chains float in the space left, the main chain (ideas -> building -> experiments -> improvements) sits at the bottom and a kept link from failures-cleared runs across the whole drawing (shots/plan-dr-is-lab-flowsonly.png). gaps.name: agent-spec-api
gaps.title: An agent's answer carries what it is: its block's definition, prompt and program files, law, machine and decisions
gaps.definition:
Problem: /api/agents/NAME (ergostat/web/server.py:557-575) returns only the mdl.Agent dataclass (model.py:165-186: name, kind, command, schedule), runs, a log tail and use, though it looks the block up at :567. On :8791 the ai block `work` has prompt: prompts/work.md and run: python3 bin/step.py work (demos/ticket-factory/steps/03-work.yaml) but the answer says only the command (spec/legacy.py:53 keeps a prompt only without a run, cut to 60 chars). The rule keep-located-worked carries no law though BlockDiagram.block_fn (blockdiagram.py:1023-1140) computes it for Blocks. The person approve has no ask. fixer's command is an absolute .venv path; improver's prompt is a package file (library/templates/modelling/template.yaml:364-395) the /file/ route (server.py:828-842) cannot serve. Decision tallies (state.decisions, state.py:459-469) are not reachable per agent.

gaps.name: goal-forecast-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: 'approaching', grace and the forecast's horizon: what a goal's word says beyond off and holding (docs/proposals/goal-forecast.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R6): a goal approaching its bound on schedule (users climbing steadily to 180) is red and 'off 100%' exactly like a failing one; a queue goal goes red each time one item waits (29 times in 33 minutes); a goal that crossed its bound 23 times reads 'holding'; the headline moves between 2 and 6 within a minute. The forecast is two clicks down, takes about 20 s, looks 4 to 8 minutes ahead whatever the window, and reads 'off at +8m15s with p≈0.07 (100 runs)' (shots/story-1-b3-loops.png, story-1-b4-ahead-users-growing.png, pm-sf-users-growing.png, sre-big-loop-osc.png). The forecast is ergostat/numbers/review.py:550 forecast(); the suggestion engine already has a verdict ('keeps up on average' against 'falling behind', state.py:524-589). Changing what 'off' counts in the headline is a semantic change and meets the completion estimates' projection (control-aware-estimates-proposal asks whether they are one model).
Change: write docs/proposals/goal-forecast.md settling: (1) the full set of the goal's one reader word (the server field `word` of goal-row-one-renderer): holding, approaching (on track to its bound from the wrong side, or about to cross from the right side), off, falling behind, flapping (filed Q18), in grace, open, unknown; which come from the projection and which from the suggestion verdict; neutral ink for approaching and in grace; the event types stay loop.off/loop.holding; and the rule that every surface (Goals rows, box rows, the Dynamics gap mark, Blocks' e label, side list, header, the Dashboard's goals panel, the evidence panel's first line) prints that one field; (2) grace and tolerance for queue goals: where declared (a goal's `for:`/tolerance keys or new ones), how said in words on the row, and that the headline counts only goals off past their grace (default, no owner question: the headline leaves out goals within a declared grace and counts them apart); (3) the horizon tied to the header's window, with 'ahead' added to the existing window menu, and its cost; (4) how the forecast is computed in the per-goal background cache (ergostat/web/goal_work.py) under one budget with the performance word, so it is on first paint; (5) the row's `expected` cell as the forecast's short form; (6) whether this projection and the items' completion estimates are one run. It confirms or amends goal-rows-say-approaching-and-expected, queue-goal-grace-in-words and forecast-on-first-paint-window-horizon.

1. The proposal settles 1-6 with the demo cases above worked through (what each reads before and after, on each surface).

gaps.name: kind-and-item-footprint-api
gaps.title: The model says what a kind and an item touch: /api/kinds/K and an item's path
gaps.definition:
Problem: no function says what a kind or an item touches in the model. /api/items gives a kind's name, states, show, description, system, relations and counts only; the rest of ItemKind (ergostat/spec/ir.py:865-889: on, fold, lease, join, final, about) never reaches a page, and an item's moves are not related to stocks, flows or blocks. The parts exist spread out: sensors counting a kind in or entering a state (spec.sensors() with .items; spec/item_sets.py:370 counted_by; spec/item_systems.py), blocks that take it with their out: flows, pool and lease (b.takes, b.targets()), goals (snap['loops']), feedback loops (spec/causal.py:242), an item's moves and fields.lease.history.
Change: new ergostat/spec/footprint.py. kind_footprint(spec, kind): definition (plain title, description, id pattern, states with which are finished via finish_of when present, on: event -> state, show, fold per field, relations both ways, join, lease rule, system and why); counted_in (each stock/auxiliary/flow whose sensor counts the kind, with states or events and system; several sensors on one state all listed); taken_by (each block: at, to, where, order, pool, attempts, TTL, out flows, agent, and how many it has taken now, a lease holder in any state); goals (those blocks' goals and goals on counted stocks, with the goal's word); loops (causal.loops through those parts, R/B and name); now (count per state). item_path(spec, item): its moves joined to the footprint as ordered steps {state, stock, flow, block, run, attempts, goal, entered, left}; `leased` is not a step; states nothing counts are said as such; nack loops and rework appear as repeated steps with attempts. GET /api/kinds/K returns the footprint (404 for an unknown kind); /api/items/ID gains path. Cached per model version; the functions read the spec only (item_path one item more), never scan the record. Snapshot includes kinds/K. Field names follow docs/vocabulary.md: taken and waiting, never held.
Definition of done:
1. On the roadmap demo's spec /api/kinds/ticket names stocks todo, in-progress, in-review, blocks developer and reviewer with their pools, goals nothing-ready-waits and in-review-clear and their loops.
2. item_path for a done roadmap ticket lists its states in order with the block that took it and attempts.
3. A kind nothing counts returns an empty footprint and a reason; a block with takes.where says it takes only some items.
4. /api/kinds/K answers under 300 ms on :8796.
5. SPEC §5a documents both.
Files: new ergostat/spec/footprint.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/snapshot.py, docs/SPEC.md, new tests/test_footprint.py.
Acceptance tests: unit tests for ticket-factory's ticket footprint (every step's stock and flow from demos/ticket-factory/steps/*.yaml and each taking block), a done ticket's path with two leases, an uncounted kind, the API 404. Each fails on main.

gaps.name: dashboard-proposal

gaps.name: dynamics-bundled-connectors-proposal

gaps.name: control-aware-estimates-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: completion estimates that run the control model and the stocks and flows together with the items (docs/proposals/control-aware-estimates.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner: 'We have a system dynamics model and a control model; a small simulation should give a real estimate of what finishes when and in what order.' ergostat/numbers/eta.py simulates items against block capacities read once at now; it knows nothing of the gates that start the blocks (the factory's implement-when: busy < min(pool, busy+room), machine-full, the AI budget goal, intake open; instance dev/model/building.yaml) or of the stocks those gates read changing over the horizon. On the factory those set throughput: pool 36 (run/pools.json) but stock.gaps-building averaged 6.1 over a day and is 1 now with 97 ready, because block.machine-full = 1. The Timeline itself says 'Not modelled: a goal that switches a block off'. numbers/closedloop.py already runs the control structure ahead on a shadow of the engine (Shadow, start_of) and is used by etamodel.gated_off only for 'off now'. It needs the estimates running on the factory record to measure anything, and the measured-concurrency model of eta-refused-takes-are-a-closed-gate as the baseline its validation bar compares against.
Change: write docs/proposals/control-aware-estimates.md settling:
1. Which control parts run inside the item simulation (expr gates evaluated through Shadow at each event or a fixed step; goals over item counts), with inputs that are item counts taken from the simulation's own state.
2. How every other input is had: kept at its newest reading, projected (simulate.project / closedloop), or driven by the items (AI spend per run, headroom per running session); the rule and how each is said in an item's why. This is the owner's one question here: keep what binds the factory's concurrency as it reads now, or project it. Default until answered: kept as it reads now, and a gap waiting on a parked gap is not scheduled.
3. Pools read from stocks that change (pool: {now: stock.X}).
4. Time coupling and the cost bound on the factory record (414 open items, 10 blocks, 200 runs); where it runs: a worker, never the web request path.
5. Whether the closed-loop risk's uncertain parameters enter the Monte Carlo.
6. One model: whether the goals' forecast (R6, goal-forecast-proposal) and the items' estimates become one projection so the Dynamics flow rate agrees with the Timeline.
7. What the Timeline and Lanes show: starts staggered by the gate, a gate's closed spans, a why naming the gate.
8. The validation bar: an ablation (Flags.control in eta.ABLATIONS) run by tests/eta_backtest.py on the factory record at past cuts (MAE of p50, p90 coverage, gaps merged in the next 24 h predicted against actual) against today's model and against the measured-concurrency model; candidate methods: stationary availability, a capacity schedule from a closed-loop projection, two-way coupling; how the record is snapshotted for a test without shipping the live record (the gated record of perf-factory-size-fixture is the CI stand-in).
9. The build split: confirm or amend control-aware-completion-estimates, with budgets.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal exists with each of the nine settled, the backtest bar as numbers and the table reproducible by a command it names.
2. A spike's measured cost of evaluating the factory's gates per event on the copied record is recorded.
3. If coupling does not improve coverage or MAE over the measured-concurrency model it recommends not coupling and says why.
4. The owner's question is asked in one sentence.
Files: docs/proposals/control-aware-estimates.md; a throwaway spike under dev/ or tests/, not shipped; at most the ablation flag stub in ergostat/numbers/eta.py and tests/eta_backtest.py.
Acceptance tests: the proposal review passes; the timing and backtest tables are in the file.
Budget: documentation; measurement code at most 150 lines.

gaps.name: agent-means-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: what a narrow AI's specification and a decision agent's means of deciding are (docs/proposals/agent-means.md)
gaps.owner_items: 19 (narrow AI's specification; a decision's means of deciding)
gaps.definition:
Problem: owner item 19 asks the Agent page to show 'for narrow AI, its specification; for decisions, the means of deciding'. The ladder hint (state.py:592-603) only infers that a decision or rule could fill a controller from what it decided (state.decisions, state.py:459-469). Problem: a system on /items draws all its kinds' charts in a grid (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:787) and only then each kind's table under an h3 at body size (pages.js:751, style.css:357): 14 px 'pr 25' under the chart. Folding is per system, open by default, in localStorage (pages.js:505-510, 625-631), and a folded system still draws and polls its charts; each chart's /api/items-flow costs about 2.5 s on the-job, so the first draw took 11 s. A state click hides every other kind's table (pages.js:247). Owner: 'the heading for an item type is hard to find'; 'every item type's list section closed by default'.

Every kind is closed on load. Open kinds are in the address (open=gap,review, replaceState); kind=K opens K and scrolls to it; a search opens the kinds it matches. Opening a kind fetches that kind alone (kind=NAME&per_kind=25 with the page's finished parameter) and draws its state chart, table and cycle chart under the bar; closed kinds ask for counts only (server: rows only for asked kinds), and the chart and list polls touch open kinds only. An open kind's bar is position: sticky under the nav. The chips are the kind's state filter: a chip click toggles that state for that kind only (state=gap:ready,fix in the address; old kind=&state= still works; a finished state's chip shows that state, as any explicit state does), restyles at once, filters loaded rows, fetches only that kind with an AbortController, and keeps the bar's place on screen. gaps.name: items-pages-through-a-kind
gaps.title: Items: an open kind pages through all its filtered items, sorted on the server, and the search reaches every item
gaps.definition:
Problem: 'All N' (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:757-758) only sets kind=, which asks 300 rows; past that the page says 'N older items not loaded' (pages.js:799). The factory has kinds of 366 and 428, the roadmap 1,180 tickets. The server already pages (n, offset; LISTED=500, ergostat/spec/items.py:30; in_states_page, spec/items.py:339, 560) but the page never asks for page 2. The search q is applied after the server cut its 500 newest (server.py:281-286), so an older item is never found and match counts are wrong. A column sort (pages.js:224-229) orders only loaded rows. Owner: 'no real pagination, so the problem returns right after clicking it'.
Change: an open kind shows 25 rows with a pager in its bar and the table's foot: '1-25 of 77 unfinished · Prev · Next' with a page size of 25, 100 or 300; the page is in the address (page=gap:3); the request is that kind, its states filter, offset and n; the poll refreshes the page shown. With a search, the kind's rows come from the index's word search (spec/items.py _paged / the existing search path) over every item of the kind, finished ones included (the rule of items-list-hides-finished-by-default: a search never hides a match), so count and pages are of all matches, with the finished ones counted apart ('3 matches, 1 finished') beside the box (filed Q32). A column sort is sent to the server (sort=gap:-ai_cost_usd), which sorts the whole filtered set (up to 5,000 items read without moves; past that the newest 5,000, said in the caption), then pages. A page past the end falls back to the last page. 'All N' and the 'older items not loaded' note are removed.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture of 1,200 items of one kind every item is reached by Next; the last page's last row is the oldest.
2. page=gap:24 in the address opens that page; a refresh on page 3 stays on page 3.
3. Searching an id that is the 1,000th newest finds it and the count reads 1; searching a finished item's id finds it with the finished filter at its default.
4. Sorting by a numeric column puts the set's global maximum (checked through the API) on page 1; the page and sort survive a reload.
5. No element with text matching /^All \d+/ or 'not loaded' exists.
6. SPEC §5a documents offset, n and sort for /api/items with one kind.
Files: ergostat/web/static/pages.js, kinds.js, style.css, ergostat/web/server.py (items handler: search for a kind via the index, offset, sort), ergostat/spec/items.py (sorted page over in_states_page), docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_items_page.py, tests/test_item_search.py or tests/test_item_index.py.
Acceptance tests: unit tests for offset + search totals and the sort cut at 6,000 items; browser tests for pager, address and sort on the roadmap fixture.
Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: diagram-routes-fast-then-refined
gaps.title: Diagram lines are drawn routed within a second and refined within a bound; fewer ELK runs, off the main thread
gaps.definition:
Problem (measured, everything open): routing is the time, not ELK. libavoid takes 0.26-1.3 s on most demos, 8.3-9.4 s on image-squeeze (:8793, 202 lines; 19 s with wrap), and does not finish in 3.5 minutes on the live factory (746 lines). On image-squeeze the same spec routes in 183 ms with crossingPenalty 0, 7.0 s at 20, 15.6 s at 80 (the page uses 50: ergostat/web/static/avoid.js:390-392, 659). ELK is 16-350 ms per run but one toggle on the-job ran it 10 times (1.6 s): the port-turn re-layout (diagram.js:197, up to twice), a second whole layout to compare (212), the wrap trial in show (1236) and the preset's retries (layouts.js:226-236). ELK runs on the main thread (util.js:6 new ELK() with no worker), so the page freezes. It needs the page guard and stand-ins of diagram-lines-stay-attached, the drop path of diagram-drag-lines-follow (a drop re-routes only its own lines on the router state the drag built: the two-stage routing must be designed against that final path and share that state), and the fixture's budgets for acceptance.
Change: (1) two-stage routing in the worker: a fast pass (crossingPenalty 0, same pins and checkpoints) answered and drawn first, then the careful pass, swapped in only if its layout is still current (the page guard's generation), no drag is in progress and none happened since it started (a drag's own re-route wins; the careful pass is then restarted on the moved places), and it has the same or fewer crossings; abandoned past 10 s (or a work estimate from line count), keeping the fast lines; a routing of a layout no longer shown is cancelled in the worker. Default, no owner question: lines may tidy themselves a second or two after the drawing appears. (2) at most 2-3 ELK runs per change: port turns decided from the graph or applied in one re-layout; the no-satellite comparison and the wrap trial only when the first layout's fit is outside their thresholds; S.layoutRuns records why each ran. (3) the last 8 layouts with their routes kept in memory, keyed by structure signature, open set, wrap, flows-only and pins: toggling back draws with no layout. (4) ELK in a Web Worker (elkjs's worker file vendored at a pinned version beside elk.bundled.js; the snapshot keeps the page path). (5) S.layout.routing distinguishes 'attached' from 'tidy' for tests and Fit.
Definition of done:
1. image-squeeze open=*: routed lines on screen 1.5 s or less after the graph arrives (today 9.7 s); on the factory graph fixture open=* attached within 3 s and careful routing finished or abandoned within 10 s.
2. A toggle and back draws the first state again in 300 ms or less with no ELK run.
3. No layout runs ELK more than 3 times (S.layoutRuns).
4. The page answers a toolbar click within 100 ms while a layout runs.
5. A drag started while the careful pass runs is never overwritten by it: after the drop every dragged part's lines end on the part.
6. The layout corpus (python -m tests.layout_corpus OUT --generated 300 against --engine of main) shows no rise in critical or major counts after refinement; any rule that gets worse is reported with crops.
Files: ergostat/web/static/avoid.js, diagram.js (layoutGraph, show), layouts.js (runLayoutWith), util.js (elk), routeparts.js, the vendored worker, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py (LAYOUT_BUDGET_MS, ROUTED_BOUND_MS lowered; the fixture's xfail turned into checks), docs/layout-rules.md, docs/proposals/scale.md row 13.
Acceptance tests: timing tests on image-squeeze and the-job; the cache test; the click-during-layout test; the drag-during-refinement test; the fixture budgets pass; the corpus comparison recorded in the commit.
Budget: 200 net lines of JS (removed passes offset some) plus 70 of tests.

gaps.name: agent-show-page
gaps.title: An Agent show page at /agent/NAME: what it is by rung (prompt, program, specification, means of deciding, law), its definition, its place, what it did
gaps.definition:
Problem: an agent has no address: /agent/work is a 404 (shots/plan-agentshow-agent-route.png; 'agent' is not in UI_PAGES, ergostat/web/server.py:35, nor in route(), static/util.js:498-512). The only view is the side panel (openAgent, static/details.js:218-252), which shows what the agent did, never what it is: on :8791 `work` shows a command, the wrong 'Runs: not run by ergostat' and an absolute log path but no prompt (plan-agentshow-work-panel.png); keep-located-worked shows no law (plan-agentshow-rule-panel.png); approve shows no ask (plan-agentshow-person-panel.png). The owner asked for the page; the request overrides 'no new pages' for it and settles R12's 'decide on Agents' (Agents stays as the index).
Change: 'agent' joins UI_PAGES (server.py, util.js); route() sends /agent/NAME to pageAgent in a new static/agent.js (index.html before main.js), following the item page's pattern. openAgent's sections move into one builder (agentSections(a)) used by panel and page, so filed Q38-Q41 land in one place. Layout:
1. h1 the name; a flowing meta line: kind (rung letter and word, rung_why as title), machine, system, serves (goal links, each with the goal's word through goalWord when goal-row-one-renderer has landed), engaged (Q38's wording), mode, defined at (file:line link).
2. 'What it is' by rung. person 'What they are asked': the ask as Markdown (md(), pages.js:247), open asks now. ai 'Its prompt': the prompt rendered, {slots} outside code marked 'filled per item'; model, tools, actions, read, workspace, emits, takes, lease as a dl; 'Its wrapper' highlighted in a closed details. narrow-ai 'Its specification': the prompt plus the fixed parts (model, outputs, max-cost). decision 'How it decides': its prompt or program, then the answers given in the window as a ranked list with counts, and the ladder hint as a sentence. program 'Its program': the command (no absolute path), each program file highlighted (code(), pages.js:180-268), the first open; an own module reads 'ergostat's own: <module>' with its docstring. rule 'Its law': law.says, the MathML (blocks.js:1010-1030) and rows; for expr each input a link with its value now; tables for lookup and schedule; 'implied by <block>'s goal' linked.
3. 'Its definition': spec.source highlighted as yaml under its file:line; implied blocks say 'not written: ergostat put it in front of <block>'.
4. 'Its place': goals and control loops it serves (each opens the goal's evidence), what commands it and what it commands, the items it is working now ('working 2 tickets', never 'holds'), 'Show on Blocks'.
5. 'What it did': runs chart, cost, Recent runs, the log tail named by relative file.
Sections are anchors; the page polls like the item page; at 390 px code scrolls in its own box. The panel gains 'Open its page'; a row on /agents navigates to /agent/NAME. web/snapshot.py includes agent pages.
Definition of done:
1. /agent/work on :8791 shows 'Its prompt' with prompts/work.md rendered (no raw '#'), {key} marked, and bin/step.py highlighted (.hljs) in a closed 'Its wrapper'; /agent/nope says 'no agent nope' with a link to /agents.
2. /agent/keep-located-worked shows 'Its law' with a math element, 'releases at', the same says text as the Blocks panel, and 'implied by work' linking to /agent/work.
3. /agent/fixer shows 'Its program' and 'ergostat's own'; no text on any /agent/* page matches /\/private\/tmp|\.venv|SPEC §/.
4. A person block shows 'What they are asked'; examples/docs-fresh /agent/page-picker shows 'How it decides' with a tally or 'no decisions in the window'.
5. At 390 px document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= 390.
6. Every agent of every demo opens with no console error and its first h2 is the rung's section name.
Files: new ergostat/web/static/agent.js, static/main.js or util.js (route), ergostat/web/server.py, static/index.html, static/details.js, static/pages.js, static/style.css, ergostat/web/snapshot.py, new tests/test_agent_page.py.
