gaps.name: dashboard-new-chart-forms
gaps.title: Three chart forms: several series on one axis, an X/Y phase plot, a heatmap over time
gaps.owner_items: 18 (several flow rates on one graph, X/Y plot, heatmap)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner asks for several flow rates on one graph, an X/Y plot of one measure against another and a heatmap. None exists: lineChart (ergostat/web/static/charts.js:192) draws one value line; cycleChart (charts.js:665) is the only point plot. /api/series already returns several refs on one time base (times, series[].values), so all three can be drawn on the client. The phase plot is listed under 'Later' in docs/proposals/charts.md; all three are recognised forms (decision 3).
Change: a new ergostat/web/static/plots.js (charts.js is 694 lines) using uPlot and the existing tokens and helpers (tok, baseOpts, mountPlot, rateUnit):
1. multiChart({times, series}): several series on one time axis, all rates in one unit (rateUnit over the largest), each line labelled at its end, line styles as well as colour telling them apart, cursor values for all.
2. phasePlot({x, y}): one series against another on the same buckets, joined in time order with direction ticks, the start an open point and the latest a filled one, axes labelled with name and unit, an optional desired level dashed on either axis.
3. heatmap({rows, times}): rows are refs (/api/series), a kind's states (/api/items-flow counts) or goals; columns are time buckets on one sequential token ramp with a scale key and the value under the cursor; an off stretch is hatched as well as coloured (filed Q76); each ref normalised to its own range is said in the key.
Each has an accessible name and a table fallback, reads in both themes, and is usable on its own until dashboard-xy-and-heatmap-panels registers it as a panel.
Definition of done:
1. multiChart for two flows of a served fixture shows two labelled lines in one unit.
2. phasePlot of one stock against another draws a joined path with its last point marked.
3. A heatmap of a kind's states has one row per state and as many columns as buckets.
4. Each renders in light and dark with no console errors, using tokens only (tests/test_style_tokens.py).
Files: new ergostat/web/static/plots.js, static/index.html (script tag), static/style.css, new tests/test_plots.py.
Acceptance tests: the three browser checks above on a test page that mounts each function with fixed data; a unit test of the bucket alignment.
Budget: 220 net lines of JS, 30 CSS, 60 tests.

gaps.name: perf-snapshot-counts-without-refolding
gaps.title: The snapshot's residual counts stop refolding every recently changed item from the record
gaps.definition:
Problem: state.snapshot -> explain (ergostat/state.py:170-191) asks moved(project, flow, t0, t1) for each counted flow of each stock; counted (state.py:99-110) passes at=t1, the stock's last reading; spec/items.py moved (279) then refolds from the record every item of the kind with an event after t1 (_late, 220) to match where fields as they stood at t1: 1,754 items in 88 calls per snapshot on the factory, plus 9,230 item unpacks (zlib + marshal). With perf-segments-item-span-first done this is most of what is left of the 0.8 s (which is why it is measured after it). Matching where as items are now measured 0.35 s but changes what a count means.
Change (pick one in the PR with the measurement): (a) within one snapshot fold each late item once, at the earliest t1 asked of its kind, and reuse it for every flow of that kind; items whose matched fields did not change between that t1 and a later one need no second fold (the index's moves say which); or (b) when now - t1 is within the stock's sensor period, match where as the items are now. (b) changes a count's meaning, so it is built only after the owner answers one sentence (open question: may a flow's item counts match 'where' against items as they are now within one sensor period?); the default is (a).
Definition of done:
1. Residuals, significant flags and estimated disturbances in the snapshot are identical to main's on all six demos' specs with seeded records and on the factory-size fixture (and, by hand in the PR, a copy of the factory state), or with (b) differ only where an item's matched field changed within the last sensor period, as listed in the PR.
2. A unit test of the chosen rule on a small record; a parity test over 24 h of recorded events.
3. Snapshot time on the factory copy under 0.45 s on one thread.
Files: ergostat/state.py, ergostat/spec/items.py (moved, _late), ergostat/spec/itemindex.py if a field history is used, tests.
Acceptance tests: the parity test and a benchmark printing before and after.
Budget: 80 net lines outside tests.

gaps.name: perf-answers-carry-only-what-is-drawn
gaps.title: The graph, the header's status poll and the item poll carry only what the page draws
gaps.definition:
Problem (measured on a copy of the factory state): the Diagram's first graph answer is 1.5 MB for two closed boxes, of which causalLoops is 1.1 MB and corr 309 KB; the header's status poll is 131 KB every 5 s per tab (loops 63 KB, check 54 KB) though the header uses only the count of goals off and the attention level (ergostat/web/static/util.js:364-374); the item page re-sends 181 KB every 6 s (history 86 KB, record 54 KB), each poll costing 1.4-2.3 s. The ETag is computed after the answer is built, so a 304 saves bytes but no work. item-page-fields-flow-and-lists-are-cards takes the history out of the item answer by default; this gap works on that answer and does not touch the history default again.
Change: (a) graph sends causalLoops only for the parts drawn (opened systems), or on ask (?loops=1) when the side panel's loop list is opened; corr likewise only when correspondence is on. (b) status?light=1 for the header: name, running, counts, goals_off, attention level; the full status stays for pages that use it. (c) the item page polls with ?since_seq=; the server answers 'unchanged' (no fold) or only the new events. Sizes are measured uncompressed (perf-compress-large-answers handles the wire).
Definition of done:
1. The Diagram's first graph answer on the factory-size fixture is under 400 KB uncompressed with systems closed.
2. The header poll is under 5 KB.
3. An unchanged item poll is under 1 KB and does no fold.
4. The render tests are green on every demo and view; loop tracing and correspondence still work once asked.
Files: ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/graph_poll.py, ergostat/web/static/util.js, diagram.js, pages.js, tests.
Acceptance tests: a size test per answer on the factory-size fixture; tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: perf-the-page-says-how-old-it-is
gaps.title: While an answer is being worked out, the page keeps what it has and says how old it is
gaps.definition:
Problem: on the live factory a page waited from 10 s to minutes with a blank table or an empty canvas and nothing said whether it was working, stale or broken (shots/plan-perf-live-diagram-1s.png, plan-perf-live-diagram-10s.png). The owner: 'they do eventually load'. Needs the answer's own `at` from perf-answers-never-wait-for-a-snapshot. Default, no owner question: the page may show values up to 15 s old as long as it says 'as of'.

Tables and diagrams keep their last content, dimmed (R8). A page waiting for its first answer shows filed Q11's 'Loading…' under the heading. The suffix uses the answer's `at`, not the browser's clock.
Definition of done:
1. With a server delayed 20 s (a test lever) the header shows the 'as of' suffix and the last content stays visible.
2. The suffix disappears on the next fresh answer.
3. At 390 px it wraps and never overflows.
Files: ergostat/web/static/util.js, main.js, style.css, a browser test.
Acceptance tests: a browser test with a delayed server for 1-3.

gaps.name: perf-page-speed-is-an-upkeep-goal
gaps.title: Page answer time is measured as an upkeep goal (web-answers-fast), with a page budget test on the factory-size fixture
gaps.definition:
Problem: the slowness was found by hand. Nothing in ergostat measures its own page, and no test catches a page that sends 97 requests or 2.5 MB (the Loops page did both). Intent decision 1 says model it rather than add UI. It needs the per-answer timing table of perf-web-requests-never-pile-up, the state directory of perf-factory-size-fixture for the budget test, and the upkeep field of goal-state-says-its-system-and-upkeep so that the new goal, made by the modelling template, is shown beside the headline and never counted in it.
Change: (a) the page server keeps two readings, answer-time p95 over the last 5 min and queue depth, exposed as built-in sensors of the modelling system (web-answer-seconds, web-queue); a default goal web-answers-fast at p95 <= 2 s (named apart from the milestone pages-answer-fast), read through the existing evidence panel. (b) a budget test loads each page (Diagram, Items, Goals, Agents, Record, Model, an item) on the factory-size fixture's served state and asserts per page: API requests on load <= 12, bytes <= 600 KB, content complete within 3 s with 5 polling tabs.
Definition of done:
1. The sensors read on every demo.
2. The goal is off when a test delays answers past 2 s, carries upkeep 'modelling', and is counted in goals_off.own, not in goals_off.system.
3. The budget test runs in CI on the fixture, fails on current main for Goals and Diagram (recorded as xfail with numbers) and passes once the perf gaps land.
Files: ergostat/web/__init__.py, ergostat/upkeep_measures.py, the modelling template, new tests/test_page_budgets.py.
Acceptance tests: the budget test; a unit test of the sensor readings; the upkeep-field assertion.
Budget: 160 net lines.

gaps.name: item-page-says-where-it-went
gaps.title: An item says where it went in the model: the stocks it was counted in and the valve and block that moved it
gaps.definition:
Problem: the item page tells leasing three times (the Lease table, 'How it moved' pairs like review -> leased -> done that lose the state it was reviewed in, raw ergostat.lease.* events; shots/plan-ks-road-item-leased.png) and never says which stocks it was counted in, which flows and valves moved it or which blocks took it; nothing links to the diagram. Each stock and valve is a link to the diagram with that part selected (filed Q36's address), each block a link to its agent page when it exists, each run a link to the Record; the final state is marked; rework shows as a repeated step with its attempt count. gaps.name: finished-rule-in-series-and-routing
gaps.title: The process map, the state counts over time and message routing take their finished states from the one function, with their outputs proved unchanged or the change said
gaps.owner_items: 4 (one answer to 'which states are done', everywhere)
gaps.definition:
Problem: items-kinds-say-which-states-finish moves the finished rule into finish_of for the Items page, the dependency graph and the estimates, and leaves three other callers on their own rules: ergostat/process.py:75-83 (done_states, also stripping 'leased'), ergostat/series.py:338 and 371-398 (state counts over time) and a separate done_states in ergostat/messages/route.py:39. Until they agree, the Items page can call a state finished that the process map draws as a middle state, or that a message's done route does not treat as done.
Change: each of the three is read and compared with finish_of on every demo spec and the factory-shaped fixture. Where its set equals finish_of's (after its own stated extras, such as stripping 'leased'), it calls finish_of and keeps the extra as one named line. Where it differs on purpose (message routing's done may be a different idea: where a message's answer goes), it keeps its rule, is renamed so it no longer reads as the same thing (e.g. route_done_states), and one SPEC sentence says how it differs. Any change in output is listed in the PR per demo and kind.
Definition of done:
1. No function named done_states remains outside ergostat/spec/finished.py and spec/itemindex.py's inference that finish_of wraps.
2. A parity test: the process map's answer, /api/series state counts and message routing's targets are byte-identical before and after on the six demos' specs with seeded records, except for the differences listed in the PR.
3. SPEC says in one place which uses share the rule and which does not, and why.
Files: ergostat/process.py, ergostat/series.py, ergostat/messages/route.py, ergostat/spec/finished.py, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_finished_states.py.
Acceptance tests: the parity test; a unit test per caller on a kind with declared done, inferred done and one state.

gaps.name: forecast-on-first-paint-window-horizon
gaps.title: The forecast is worked out with the page in the per-goal background cache, and looks as far ahead as the window says
gaps.definition:
Problem (R6 pieces 5 and 7): the forecast is two clicks down, takes about 20 s when asked, and looks 4 to 8 minutes ahead whatever the window (shots/story-1-b3-users-detail.png, pmb-sf-users-stock.png). To be on rows and boxes it must exist before anyone asks, without making every answer wait and without adding a second goal-by-goal worker to a process the perf milestone is unloading.
Change, as the proposal settles: the forecast per goal (ergostat/numbers/review.py:550) is an entry kind of the per-goal background cache that perf-goals-page-asks-once built (ergostat/web/goal_work.py), keyed (goal, 'forecast', window, horizon); the cache's one pass runs on the snapshot thread's after_snapshot hook (perf-answers-never-wait-for-a-snapshot) and does the performance word and the forecast under one stated time budget per pass, off goals first, resuming where it stopped. The loops answer carries each goal's forecast with its age; a goal not yet done says 'being worked out'. No request computes a forecast. The horizon is tied to the header's window (e.g. half the window ahead, as the proposal decides), and the existing window menu (ergostat/web/static/main.js:6) gains 'ahead' choices; the choice is in the address (filed Q36). Charts that show a projection draw it to that horizon.
Definition of done:
1. On a served fixture, after the server has been up 60 s, /api/loops carries a forecast for every goal and the page makes no forecast request.
2. Changing the window changes the horizon stated in every forecast sentence.
3. No /api request takes longer because a forecast is stale (p95 unchanged against perf-answers-never-wait-for-a-snapshot's test), and the process has one goal-by-goal worker (a test counts the threads and the budget per pass).
4. On the factory-size fixture every goal's forecast is refreshed within the proposal's budget.
Files: ergostat/web/goal_work.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/numbers/review.py, ergostat/web/static/main.js, util.js, charts.js, tests.
Acceptance tests: a unit test of the cache entries, the shared budget and the 'being worked out' state; a browser test for 2; the timing check.
Budget: 140 net lines.

gaps.name: goal-rows-say-approaching-and-expected
gaps.title: A goal's one word gains 'approaching' and 'falling behind' in neutral ink, its row an 'expected' cell, and every surface prints the same word
gaps.definition:
Problem (R6 pieces 3 and 6): a goal approaching its bound on schedule is red and 'off 100%' exactly like a failing one (users climbing to 180 on software-factory: shots/story-1-b4-ahead-users-growing.png, pm-sf-users-ahead.png); the Goals page's 'back in' column cannot say what to expect. If only some surfaces learn the new word, a goal would read 'approaching' on Goals, 'off' in red on its Dynamics gap and 'e = -7 off' in Blocks: story B3's failure, split across views. The cached forecast (forecast-on-first-paint-window-horizon) is needed, or each row would cost about 20 s.
Change, as the proposal settles: the server function that makes each goal's `word` (goal-row-one-renderer) combines its status, the cached projection and the suggestion engine's verdict (ergostat/state.py:524-589): 'approaching' (heading to its bound), 'falling behind', beside holding, off, flapping (filed Q18), open, unknown. Event types and the status field stay. The row's `expected` field is the forecast's short form (forecast-sentence-in-words) and its `trend` the word from one function ('getting worse', 'recovering', 'steady'). goalRow draws 'expected' in place of 'back in'. Because every surface prints `word` through goalWord or goalRow (the rule and grep test of goal-row-one-renderer), the Goals page, the side list, the box rows, the Dynamics gap mark, Blocks' e label, the header's tooltip, the Dashboard's goals panel and the evidence panel's first line change together, with one ink rule (docs/DESIGN.md): approaching in the neutral token, off and falling behind in --bad outside Blocks. The headline's count follows the proposal's rule through state.goals_off. The Guide frame that explains a goal's states lists the words.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture with a goal climbing on schedule, it reads 'approaching' in the neutral token, not --bad, on the Goals page and the side list.
2. A goal whose projection never reaches its bound reads 'falling behind' in the alarm colour.
3. Each row's 'expected' cell equals the panel's forecast short form.
4. Agreement test: for every goal of the fixture, at one moment, the word printed on every surface that exists in the build (Goals row, side list, box row, Dynamics gap mark, Blocks e label, Dashboard goals panel, evidence first line) equals /api/loops' word.
Files: ergostat/state.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/static/goalrow.js, pages.js, style.css, ergostat/guide.py, tests/test_runner_and_state.py, tests/test_graph_cli_web.py, a browser test.
Acceptance tests: unit: the word for an on-schedule, a failing and a flapping fixture; browser: 1, 3 and the agreement test.
Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: queue-goal-grace-in-words
gaps.title: A queue goal states its grace and tolerance in words, and the headline counts only goals off past their grace
gaps.definition:
Problem (R6 piece 4): a queue goal ('nothing waits') goes red each time one item waits: 29 times in 33 minutes on ticket-factory, and the headline moves between 2 and 6 within a minute (shots/pm-job-loops-4s.png, story-1-b3-backlog-detail.png). A goal that is off for four seconds while its agent picks the item up is working as designed. The count must change in one place only (state.goals_off, which headline-one-function-everywhere makes every surface print), or the numbers split again.
Change, as the proposal settles: a goal may carry a grace (off only after the bound has been crossed for that long) and a tolerance, declared where the proposal says; the engine's loop.off event and actuation are unchanged unless the proposal says otherwise. The goal's `word` within grace is 'in grace' (neutral ink), with the row saying 'off 4s of 60s'. The row prints the rule in words ('nothing waits longer than 1 min') as part of its bound. state.goals_off excludes goals within grace from system and own and counts them under in_grace; because the header, the switcher, the side list, the Goals heading and the CLI all print that one function's numbers, none is edited beyond showing the extra count in a title. The modelling template's and the demos' queue goals get sensible graces (this is the first gap to add a grace to requests-handled).
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture queue goal with waits shorter than its grace, over 10 minutes the headline's count never changes because of them (sampled each 5 s).
2. A queue goal's row states its grace in words; within grace its word is 'in grace' on every surface (the agreement test of goal-rows-say-approaching-and-expected, extended, when that has landed).
3. /api/status goals_off excludes goals within grace and counts them under `in_grace`; `ergostat status` prints the same.
4. SPEC documents the key and the wording; `ergostat check` accepts it.
Files: ergostat/spec/compile.py and ir.py (if a key is added), ergostat/state.py (word, goals_off), ergostat/web/static/goalrow.js, the modelling template and demos' queue goals, docs/SPEC.md, tests.
Acceptance tests: unit: a goal off for less than its grace is in_grace, past it off; the sampled headline test on the fixture.
Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: box-rows-trend-and-where-heading
gaps.title: Each goal row on a box shows its trend and where it is heading
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1 pieces 4 and 6): a row with value and bound says where a goal is, not whether it is getting worse or what to expect; the module panel's 'Its measures, on one time axis' already holds the data (shots/pmb-sf-users-panel.png) and the Goals page's sparkline column is the same row (newcomer-briefed-tf-loops.png). The data must already be there: the points come on the loops answer (perf-goals-page-asks-once), the forecast from the background cache (forecast-on-first-paint-window-horizon) and its wording from forecast-sentence-in-words; this gap builds none of them again.
Change: the compact form of goalRow on a box (dynamics-box-goal-rows) gains two cells that the row's fields already carry: (a) a sparkline over the header's window with the bound as a dashed line, from the points on the loops answer, and the row's `trend` word ('getting worse', 'recovering', 'steady'; the one server function; if goal-rows-say-approaching-and-expected has not landed, this gap adds that function and it reuses it); (b) a last cell from the row's `expected` field ('back by 14:10', 'crosses its bound in about 2h', 'no estimate'), shown only when the cached forecast exists (it fills on a later poll; never a request per row). The Goals page shows the same cells through the same function.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture each row of a closed box has a sparkline with a dashed bound and a trend word; the word agrees with the Goals page's row for the same goal.
2. The heading cell appears without any extra request on load and matches the evidence panel's forecast sentence.
3. Off is a mark as well as a colour on the sparkline (filed Q76).
4. No text under 11 px; the box's rows still fit at 1440 px on :8797.
Files: ergostat/web/static/goalrow.js, dynamics.js, charts.js (row sparkline), ergostat/state.py (trend, if not yet there), style.css, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: a browser test for 1-2 on a fixture goal trending toward its bound; a unit test of the trend word function.
Budget: 100 net lines.

gaps.name: closed-box-shows-items-inside
gaps.title: A closed system shows the total of the items counted inside it
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1 piece 7, story F4): a stock above zero inside a closed system is invisible from outside; the reader must open the system to learn that 37 tickets sit in it. The items counted by a system's stocks are known (ergostat/spec/item_systems.py places each kind in a system by the sensors that count it; spec/item_sets.py counted_by).
Change: each closed box (Dynamics and Blocks) prints one muted line per item kind counted inside it, unfinished items only: '37 tickets (3 being worked)', at most two kinds then 'and N more kinds'; the line links to that kind's items on the Items page (an item set, shown exactly per the item-set rule, so the list's count equals the line's). The count comes with the graph answer from the item index's state counts (no listing), and updates with the values poll. A system counting no items prints nothing.
Definition of done:
1. On ticket-factory the factory box shows its tickets' unfinished total, equal to the sum of /api/items counts for the kind's unfinished states.
2. The link opens the Items page on that kind and lists as many items as the line says.
3. A system with no counted kind shows no line.
4. No extra request on load (network test).
Files: ergostat/dynamics.py or ergostat/fold.py (system node), ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, blocks.js, tests/test_dynamics_view.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: a unit test of the system node's item totals; a browser check on ticket-factory and the roadmap fixture.
Budget: 60 net lines.

gaps.name: phone-home-is-the-stacked-boxes
gaps.title: On a phone the stacked system boxes are the home view; the redirect to the goals list goes
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1 piece 8): at phone width '/' redirects to the goals list (ergostat/web/static/main.js:53) because the diagram is unreadable there; on the-job the first screen is then two red rows, both modelling's (shots/plan-goalvocab-8792-phone-home.png, story-4-phone-job.png). The redirect in main.js:53 is removed. Above the boxes the panel order of diagram-side-panel-legend-first applies ('Waiting for you' first when something waits, with filed Q43's header link); filed Q73 (fitted on load) still applies.
Definition of done:

2. On a fixture with a planted off goal, it is visible in its box without a tap.

gaps.name: evidence-panel-reads-as-a-runbook
gaps.title: A goal's evidence opens with its four lines, then the charts, then parts and prose; the remedy comes from its suggestion
gaps.owner_items: R7 piece 7 (pieces 1-6 are filed Q26, Q28-Q31, Q33, Q34, Q36)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R7 piece 7): the evidence panel is the best thing in the product (y with r, u and e on one time axis, crossings, decisions) and every reviewer said to keep it, but it answers an SRE's questions in a modeller's order and words: parts and prose first, 'Not worked out: it has no one process', the remedy elsewhere under Suggestions (shots/story-2-c1-evidence.png, story-2-c5-evidence.png, sreb-job-loop-panel.png).
Change: reorder openLoop's panel (ergostat/web/static/details.js:140 onward, control.js): (1) four lines first, each one sentence: what is wanted and where it is now (the goal's word through goalWord, bound written per filed Q23, the distance in the one phrase of one-phrase-for-how-far-off when landed); how long off against how long it usually takes (filed Q29); what acts on it and whether it was commanded, ran and moved (filed Q28's line); what to expect (the forecast sentence when present); (2) the remedy line: the suggestion for this goal from the snapshot's hints (ergostat/state.py:524-589), shown only when it has a verdict (filed Q80's rule), with its Evidence link; (3) the charts; (4) parts, the control-loop table (filed Q69) and the prose, with 'Not worked out: it has no one process' reworded to what a reader can do. The lines are built by functions the quick fixes own, in whatever order they land: this gap only orders and adds the remedy and expectation lines.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture an off goal's panel has, before any chart, four one-sentence lines and (when a suggestion with a verdict exists) one remedy line.
2. The charts follow; parts and prose come last.
3. The remedy text equals the Suggestions entry for that goal; the first line's word equals /api/loops' word.
4. No sentence in the first screen of the panel contains 'Not worked out'.
5. At 390 px the four lines fit without horizontal scroll.
Files: ergostat/web/static/details.js, control.js, style.css, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.

gaps.name: dashboard-page-v1
gaps.title: The Dashboard page: panels drawn from existing components, arranged by its address
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner's information is spread over the Items page (scrolling) and the Diagram's side panels (panning and zooming); the components exist but are reachable only inside their pages (shots/plan-dash-sf-items.png, plan-dash-sf-users-panel.png, plan-dash-tf-timeline.png).
Change: add /dashboard as docs/proposals/dashboard.md decides, with the panel kinds that reuse existing renderers. This gap draws an arrangement; it has no editor (adding, moving, resizing and removing panels is dashboard-add-and-edit-draft), and it shows no YAML.
1. Route: 'dashboard' in UI_PAGES (ergostat/web/server.py:35, static/util.js:15), the route table (util.js:508), OTHER_PAGES (split.js:26), the nav after Diagram and the script list (index.html:12). '/' stays the folded diagram.
2. New files static/dashboard.js (page and grid) and panels.js (registry: type -> {params, load, draw, href}); nothing added to pages.js beyond moving out what panels need.
3. Panels: note (md()); goals (rows drawn by goalRow from goalrow.js, the same rows as the Goals page and the boxes; its counts from goals_off; cards on a phone); items by kind or filter (itemsSection refactored to accept plain item-set params, keeping its callers; first 10 rows, 'all N on the Items page' linking to the same set); states over time (flowChart over /api/items-flow); cycle time; chart (lineChart over /api/series; with projection the replay and fan as the stock panel draws them); goal scope (loopScope); items graph and timeline (relGraph/relTimeline over /api/items-graph). Any panel that prints a goal's state prints the server's word through goalWord.
4. Under each chart the model's reading in a line: value against bound, when the projection crosses it.
5. The arrangement is read from the address (?d=..., the proposal's compact form); with none, the proposal's default (the off goals' scopes, each kind's states chart, the busiest kind's unfinished list). 'Copy link' copies the address.
6. Load: the header's window and moment for every panel; all plain series refs in one /api/series call per refresh; replay/fan panels loaded only on screen (IntersectionObserver) and polled at the proposal's interval; no polls while hidden.
7. Each panel has a title, its source in words, a link to the full view with the same params, 'Loading…' at once and a clear empty state; panels are reachable by Tab in reading order with their title as accessible name.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 /dashboard with a 6-panel ?d= shows 6 titled panels within 1 s and each link opens its page with the same params.
2. Reload and a fresh browser given the same address draw the same panels.
3. The network log shows one /api/series call for all plain series panels; a projection panel below the fold makes no replay request until scrolled into view.
4. At 390 px one column and no horizontal scroll; light and dark use tokens only.
5. The page makes no POST and contains no YAML text.
6. The goals panel's rows have the same cells and words as the Goals page's rows for the same goals (compared in one test).

Acceptance tests: Playwright tests for the six points in the style of tests/test_items_page.py.
Budget: 330 net lines of JS, 50 CSS, 110 tests.

gaps.name: dashboard-declaration-and-api
gaps.title: Named dashboards declared under dashboards: in the model, checked like show:, and served in one request
gaps.definition:
Problem: an arrangement in the address is personal; a shared dashboard needs a durable home whose references are checked, so a renamed stock is a finding instead of a blank panel. Fetching panels one by one would load a server that already stops answering on the factory. Precedent: systems.*.show is a display declared in the model, compiled with its references checked (ergostat/spec/compile.py:908-913, 1588; SPEC §4a). Built only if the proposal and the owner's answer keep declared dashboards.
Change (as the proposal decides): (1) a top-level dashboards: NAME: {description, window?, panels: [{type, title, size, params}]} in spec/compile.py and ir.py, schema/ergostat.schema.json and SPEC §4; unknown types or keys and references to unknown stocks, flows, auxiliaries, goals, kinds or states are errors with file and line; a dashboard in a system's file is namespaced by that system. (2) GET /api/dashboards lists name, description and panel count. (3) GET /api/dashboard/NAME returns each panel's declaration and answer, built by the functions the existing endpoints call (series plus add_to_series; the items listing through item_sets; items-flow; items-graph plus eta; the loops rows), all on one Live.snapshot with a per-panel time limit (over it: {pending: true}, computed for the next poll) and have= stamps so an unchanged panel is not re-sent. NAME=default gives the model-derived one (each top system's show: measures and its goals). (4) `ergostat snapshot` holds each dashboard's answer. (5) /dashboard lists the named dashboards beside the reader's own when dashboard-page-v1 is present; a declared one is read-only with 'Copy to mine'. (6) docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md says how an agent or the Supervisor adds one (people do not write it by hand); SPEC says whether a dashboards-only change skips the judge's replay.
Definition of done:
1. The key loads, validates and round-trips; a spec naming stock.nope fails `ergostat check` with unknown-ref at its line.
2. One request returns every panel, and its answers equal the separate endpoints' for the same snapshot.
3. A panel forced slow answers pending while the others answer.
4. On :8796 GET /api/dashboard/default takes under 0.5 s.
5. The page has no control that writes a declared dashboard.
Files: ergostat/spec/compile.py, ergostat/spec/ir.py, schema/ergostat.schema.json, ergostat/web/server.py, new ergostat/web/dashboard_api.py, ergostat/web/snapshot.py, docs/SPEC.md, docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, a dashboards: block in the software-factory and ticket-factory demos, tests.
Acceptance tests: compile tests (parse, namespacing, bad reference), API tests (batched equals separate; slow panel pending), the timing check.
Budget: 400 net lines including tests; the Coordinator may split it as (a) the key, schema and check, (b) the batched API.

gaps.name: dynamics-module-bundled-connectors
gaps.title: Dynamics: connectors between two closed modules drawn as one bundle
gaps.definition:
Problem: on ticket-factory with factory and modelling open 21 connectors run between closed modules in 7 pairs, cables of up to 6 parallel lines with stacked signs (shots/plan-notation-tf-dyn-open-dark.png); on :8796 top level 6-7 lines in 2 pairs. Dynamics gives each crossing part its own port (ergostat/fold.py:112-137) and never merges lines (dynamics.py:320-432).
Change, as docs/proposals/dynamics-bundled-connectors.md settles (its default reading here). This gap builds the one bundle representation the proposal defines (the edge kind, its members, its panel); dynamics-trunk-bundling-in-open-systems reuses it and adds nothing parallel. In ergostat/dynamics.py finish(), after shadows(), group connectors whose source and target are both system nodes with ports by (source, target, flow-or-information). Each group at or over the threshold becomes one edge of kind 'bundle' carrying members [{id, from, to, polarity, sourcePort, targetPort, causal}] and n; member ports keep their rows, ordered so a bundle's rows are adjacent (diagram.js:45-46), and each end gets one bundle port. correspond.py makes the bundle stand for its members' parts. dynamics.js draws the bundle in the proposal's glyph with its mark; each member keeps its own head and sign on its unshared end; clicking the bundle opens a panel listing each member link with its sign, each a link to its parts. Loop highlighting (sdApply, dynamics.js:400) lights a bundle when any member is in the loop and the panel says how many. Flows only keeps a bundle only when a kept member is in it. diagram.js gives ELK one port per bundle (diagram.js:97-101) and redraws it after a drag (diagram.js:602). Legend row, the Guide frame that shows modules, and export. Filed Q25's sign test is amended as the proposal says.
Definition of done:
1. On :8791 diagram?open=factory,modelling no two connector paths join the same pair of modules; drawn module-to-module lines equal the number of pairs (7 against 21).
2. Each bundle shows its mark and its panel lists every member with its sign.
3. Hovering a loop row whose loop runs through a member lights that bundle.
4. Flows only hides a bundle with no flow member; correspondence colours ring the bundle; it is keyboard-reachable like other lines.
5. Dragging a module redraws the bundle attached to it.
6. SPEC's module paragraph (near docs/SPEC.md:3777) describes it.
Files: ergostat/dynamics.py, ergostat/correspond.py, ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, diagram.js, style.css, export.js, ergostat/guide.py, tests/test_dynamics_view.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/SPEC.md.
Acceptance tests: a unit test of finish() (threshold, members kept, ports adjacent, a part feeding two modules); a browser test on :8791 counting module-to-module paths and opening one bundle's panel.
Budget: 250 net lines.

gaps.name: diagram-draws-what-an-item-or-kind-touches
gaps.title: The Dynamics and Blocks diagrams draw only what an item passed through, or what a kind touches
gaps.definition:
Problem: owner item 20: 'the subset of the Dynamics and Blocks diagrams it passed through'. /api/graph draws an explicit subset only through around= (one part and its neighbours, ergostat/graph.py:19, server.py:512) and only in Dynamics; Blocks (blockdiagram.diagram, blockdiagram.py:1423) takes only open_ and focus.

The Diagram page shows a chip ('what ticket/SCRUM-2 passed through ×', like the around chip at diagram.js:1118), numbers each stock on an item's path in move order and prints attempts on each valve. The item page's 'Where it went' gains 'Draw its path in Dynamics' and 'in Blocks' links (/diagram?view=dynamics&item=ID); the kind's footprint is reachable as &kind=K.

2. view=blocks&item=... draws the control loops it touched, each whole.
3. kind=ticket draws the kind's footprint.
4. An item of a kind nothing counts shows 'not counted anywhere in the model' and no link.
5. Clearing the chip draws the diagram as before; no console errors; layout time for a subset on the factory graph fixture under 1 s.
6. SPEC's diagram section documents item= and kind=.

Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: the-kind-page
gaps.title: The kind's page: its definition, where the model counts and moves it, its goals and loops, and its items
gaps.definition:
Problem: owner item 15: 'no page representative of an item type ... its definition, the stocks and flows related to it, the feedback loops and control loops it takes part in, a well-designed filter, what all is this item?' Today the kind link goes to /items?kind=K (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:699), which only filters the list (shots/plan-ks-road-items-ticket.png): the description sits small on the system heading, the states are legend chips, and nothing names the kind's stocks, flows, taking blocks, goals or loops.
Change, as docs/proposals/item-and-kind-footprint.md decided (default: the Items page with exactly one kind chosen, at /items/<kind>, /items?kind=K redirecting with its other params, no new nav entry). Filled from /api/kinds/K, in order:
1. The kind's bar, drawn by the same kindBar function in static/kinds.js that the Items page uses, with the same markup (title, id pattern small, description, 'finishes: merged, closed' or 'lives on', state chips with counts, 'in <system>' with why on hover); here the title is the page's h1 and the list below is open. On the Items page the bar's title links here; the disclosure there still opens the list in place. Filtering by chip behaves identically on both.
2. Now: the state chart and cycle time under the bar; finished states folded per the page's one finished parameter.
3. In the model: a table of counted in (stock, which states), moved by (flow, which events), taken by (block: at, to, where, pool now and at most, attempts, TTL, taken and waiting now), goals (each with its word through goalWord), feedback loops (R/B and name); every name links to the diagram with that part selected or to the goal's evidence; links 'its states as a process map' (view=process&kinds=K, filed Q57's content) and 'draw what it touches' (kind=K) when that gap has landed.
4. Definition, a closed details: events -> states, fields shown, how each folds, relations both ways, joins, the lease rule.
5. Items: the list section, filter and pager built by the Items-list gaps, reused, not redesigned. Graph and Timeline stay views of the list.
Every link to a kind (item page header, Items bar titles, process map, stock panels' 'Show them on the Items page' when it names a whole kind) points to the kind's page.
Definition of done:
1. On the roadmap demo /items/ticket has h1 'ticket', its description, 'finishes', and an 'In the model' table naming todo, in-progress, in-review, developer, reviewer, nothing-ready-waits and its loops, each a link whose href starts with /diagram or opens evidence.
2. /items?kind=ticket ends at /items/ticket; the item page's kind link and the Items page's bar title go there.
3. The bar on /items/ticket and the ticket bar on /items have the same markup apart from the heading level and the open state (a test compares them); a chip click filters the list in place on both (window.__same survives) and lands in the address.
4. A kind nothing counts says so in section 3 and still shows its definition and items; built-in kinds render.
5. At 390 px every section stacks with no horizontal scroll.
6. SPEC §5a describes the kind's page; existing Items tests pass or are updated with the reason.
Files: ergostat/web/static/kinds.js, pages.js, main.js or util.js (route), ergostat/web/server.py (route), style.css, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_items_page.py.
Acceptance tests: test_a_kinds_page_shows_its_definition_and_model_place, test_the_kind_bar_is_one_component, test_a_kinds_state_link_filters_without_reload, test_an_uncounted_kind_says_so, the redirect test. Each fails on main.
Budget: 300 net lines; if over, split definition and model place from the list wiring.

gaps.name: agent-names-link-to-their-page
gaps.title: Every agent name links to its page, and Agents rows are links
gaps.definition:
Problem: agent names are plain text everywhere except the Agents table, where a row click opens a panel (ergostat/web/static/pages.js:100, a tr onclick: no focus, no new tab; filed Q47 records a re-sort opening the wrong agent). On :8791 the item page's lease table shows 'close', 'merge', 'ci', 'review' in its block column as text (shots/plan-agentshow-item-pattern.png); Recent runs, Actions 'by', the evidence actor line and Blocks captions likewise.

On /agents the name cell is agentLink; a plain click on the row outside the link still opens the panel. The item page's lease table block column, the Actions table's 'by' and 'approved by' (when a block), the evidence actor line (filed Q28/Q30 wherever it lands), the goal panel's controller and actuator names, the Blocks definition panel's 'block' row and the valve panel's list of taken items use it. The Record's machine filter (?machine=NAME) links back to the agent page in its scope line.

1. On :8791/agents each row's first cell contains an a with href /agent/<its name>, reachable by Tab.
2. On /item/ticket%2FSCRUM-7 every non-empty cell of the lease table's block column is a link to /agent/.
3. On the Blocks panel for a machine block the agent's name is a link to /agent/.
4. A test listing the agent names asserts each occurrence in those containers is inside an a.
Files: ergostat/web/static/util.js or details.js (helper), pages.js, details.js, blocks.js, itemsets.js, a Playwright test.
Acceptance tests: the four points on :8791 and :8792 (structure only).

gaps.name: eta-calibration-said-on-the-timeline
gaps.title: The Timeline says how well past estimates held: 'last week, 8 in 10 gaps finished by their p90'
gaps.definition:
Problem: a Gantt is believed only if its past forecasts held. tests/eta_backtest.py measures coverage, MAE and bias by replaying past cuts of the record, but only in tests; the page gives no reason to trust 'expected Tue 14:10' and no warning when estimates are poor (e.g. coverage 0.4 on a kind whose runs changed). Needs estimates that run on the record.
Change: move the backtest's core (read at a cut with truth, simulate, score) from tests/eta_backtest.py into ergostat/numbers/etacheck.py (the test imports it). The eta worker (ergostat/web/eta_api.py) runs it at most once an hour per kind asked, on 4 cuts over the last 7 days, runs=100, within its own budget and off the request path, cached beside the estimates. merge() adds eta.calibration[kind] = {coverage, items, mae, since}. The Timeline note adds one clause per kind: 'last week's estimates: 8 in 10 gaps finished by their p90 (41 gaps)'; fewer than 10 items: 'too few finished last week to check'; coverage under 0.7: the clause in the warning ink. SPEC §5a says this.
Definition of done:
1. The calibration is worked out by the worker, never on a request: no /api/items-graph request takes longer when it is stale.
2. One clause per kind on the Timeline; warned when poor.
3. The tests use the same code path.
Files: new ergostat/numbers/etacheck.py, tests/eta_backtest.py, ergostat/web/eta_api.py, ergostat/web/static/relations.js, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_eta.py.
Acceptance tests: on tests/test_eta.py's owners_record calibration coverage lies in [0.8, 1.0] and the note contains 'finished by their p90'; a record with 3 finished items says 'too few finished last week to check'.
Budget: 80 net lines (moved lines not counted).

gaps.name: dashboard-xy-and-heatmap-panels
gaps.title: The Dashboard gains several-series, X/Y and heatmap panels
gaps.definition:
Problem: dashboard-page-v1 ships the panels whose renderers existed; the owner also listed several flow rates on one graph, an X/Y plot and a heatmap. dashboard-new-chart-forms builds the three chart functions in static/plots.js but they are not panels.
Change: register three panel types in ergostat/web/static/panels.js: multi (refs: [...], one /api/series call shared with the other series panels; rates in one unit per filed Q20/Q21), xy (x: ref, y: ref; the model's replay path dashed over the measured one when either part is modelled; goal bounds as reference lines) and heatmap (rows: goals | a kind's states | a list of refs). Each has a title link to the source (the part's panel on /diagram, the kind's items, /goals), the shared time cursor (heatmap: the time column) and the model's-reading line under it. Their params editors belong to dashboard-add-and-edit-draft (whichever lands second adds the three). If dashboards are declared in the model, the three types are added to the compile check's known panel types.
Definition of done:
1. On a served fixture a dashboard with a multi panel of three flows draws three labelled lines in one unit from one /api/series request.
2. An xy of one stock against a flow draws a path ending at the current values shown in that stock's panel.
3. On a fixture with a goal carrying a planted off stretch (the factory-size fixture's, or a small seeded record: never a live demo's modelling goal, which other gaps make hold), a heatmap of goals shows that stretch as hatched cells at the same times as its scope's off bands.
4. All three work at 390 px and in dark.
Files: ergostat/web/static/panels.js, dashboard.js, plots.js (hooks only), ergostat/spec/compile.py (known types, if present), tests/test_dashboard_page.py.
Acceptance tests: the three browser checks above.
Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: dashboard-add-and-edit-draft
gaps.title: The Dashboard's draft is edited in the page and filled from anywhere: add, move, resize, remove, by mouse or keyboard
gaps.definition:
Problem: dashboard-page-v1 draws an arrangement given in the address but offers no way to make one except by writing the address by hand. The owner wants configurable panels; people do not write configuration (decision 7; the owner's rule that the Supervisor writes config), so the draft must be made by pointing, never by editing text, and nothing here writes a file. charts.js 'your charts' (charts.js:493-500) already keeps a per-browser draft of 3 parts. This gap is the only place panel editing lives.
Change: (1) 'Add to dashboard' on every stock, flow and auxiliary chart, every goal row, every item list or filtered /items view and the Timeline adds the matching panel to the draft. (2) each panel's menu edits its subject (picked from the model's names, never typed as a reference), kind where it applies, size and order, and removes it; panels can be moved and resized by pointer and by keyboard (the menu's Move up/down/left/right and Wider/Narrower/Taller/Shorter; arrow keys while the panel's handle is focused), with focus returned to the panel after each change and each change announced (aria-live) (story H5). (3) the draft is held in the address (compact, shareable) and in localStorage per project and written nowhere on the server; 'your charts' becomes the draft; 'Copy link' shares it. No YAML is shown or copied. (4) the editors for every registered panel type, including multi, xy and heatmap when present.
Definition of done:
1. The page makes no POST and writes no file.
2. From an empty draft, 'Add to dashboard' on a stock's chart and on a filtered Items view gives a dashboard with those two panels; the draft survives reload, and its link opened in a fresh browser draws the same panels.
3. Keyboard only: a panel is added from the page's own 'Add panel' menu, moved, resized and removed, and focus is on a sensible element after each step.
4. A subject is chosen from a list of the model's names; no free-text reference field exists.
Files: ergostat/web/static/dashboard.js, panels.js, charts.js, itemsets.js, pages.js, relations.js, goalrow.js (the row's add control), style.css, tests/test_dashboard_page.py.
Acceptance tests: browser tests for 1-4 on a served fixture.
Budget: 250 net lines.

gaps.name: dashboard-keep-display-proposal
gaps.title: Keep: a dashboard draft becomes a declared dashboard through an owner display proposal
gaps.definition:
Problem: a draft lives in one browser and its links; a dashboard the owner wants kept needs to reach the model's dashboards: without a person writing configuration (decision 7). The what-if (ergostat/web/numbers_api.py post: propose, then accept) is the allowed page path from an owner proposal to a YAML write. Build only if the proposal and the owner's answer say Keep goes through the page; otherwise this gap is amended to 'the Supervisor writes it from the draft's link' and shrinks to a documented Supervisor step in docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md.
Change: 'Keep' on a draft makes an ergostat.model-change of kind display, made by owner, carrying the diff of dashboards: (worked out by the server from the draft, never shown as text to edit), shown as a proposal; the judge passes display changes at once (no dynamics changed); Accept writes the YAML through the same path as a what-if; Dismiss drops it. Agents' and the Supervisor's display proposals appear the same way.
Definition of done:
1. The page writes no file except through Accept.
2. Keep then Accept gives a declared dashboard that `ergostat check` passes and /api/dashboards lists.
3. The model-change item records owner as the maker.
4. A display change is never replayed by the judge and a change touching anything but dashboards: is refused as display.
Files: ergostat/web/static/dashboard.js, ergostat/web/numbers_api.py (a display proposal), the judge's policy for kind display, docs/SPEC.md (dashboards section and the model-change table), docs/AGENT-GUIDE.md, tests.
Acceptance tests: browser on a served fixture: Keep makes one model-change of kind display; after Accept /dashboard draws it; the refusal unit test.
Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: dashboard-diagram-panel
gaps.title: A diagram in a Dashboard panel: a Diagram or Items Graph address drawn read-only
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner wants a nodes-and-edges diagram on the dashboard. The model diagram runs on page-global state S with an ELK layout and is embedded today only as a whole page in an iframe with ?pane=1 (ergostat/web/static/split.js:1-40); layout is slow on large models (owner item 10), so a dashboard poll must never re-lay it.
Change: a diagram panel takes a Diagram address (view dynamics, blocks or process; system; opened; selection; item= or kind= when available) or an Items Graph address (kinds or system). The Items Graph draws through relGraph directly. The model diagram is drawn read-only and fitted, by the embedding the proposal chose: the existing ?pane=1 frame with toolbar and side panel hidden, or an embeddable entry point in diagram.js with its own state object if the proposal's cost check allows. Values update in place through graph_poll; no re-layout while the structure signature is unchanged (the layout cache of diagram-routes-fast-then-refined is used when present). At most one model-diagram panel is live per dashboard (others draw on click), nothing loads until the panel is on screen, and clicking opens the full page at that address. Text is never drawn under 11 px: when the drawing will not fit, the panel shows the closed boxes and says 'open on the Diagram'.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 a panel for view=dynamics&system=product draws within 3 s, and on the next poll redraws values without calling layout (asserted by a counter).
2. On :8797 a whole-model panel shows the folded boxes, not unreadable text.
3. The click opens the same address.
4. No console errors on any demo; no elk request before the panel is on screen.
Files: ergostat/web/static/panels.js, dashboard.js, diagram.js or split.js (the embedding), ergostat/web/graph_poll.py if needed, tests/test_dashboard_page.py.
Acceptance tests: the browser checks for 1-4.
Budget: 220 net lines.

gaps.name: item-page-draws-its-path
gaps.title: The item page draws its path on the Dynamics and Blocks diagrams, on demand
gaps.owner_items: 20 (the subset of the diagrams, on the item page)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner asks to see, on the item page itself, the subset of the Dynamics and Blocks diagrams an item leased to agents passed through. diagram-draws-what-an-item-or-kind-touches gives the subset on the Diagram page and links to it; the item page still shows no picture. diagram.js (pageDiagram and its drawers) runs on the page-global S, #detail and pins, so it cannot be mounted elsewhere as it is. Build this as docs/proposals/item-and-kind-footprint.md decided (inline on demand is the default; if the proposal chose links only, close this gap).
Change: under 'Where it went' a closed section 'Draw its path' with a Dynamics/Blocks switch. Opening it draws item=ID in a box about 420 px high, full width, fitted, with no toolbar, side panel, pins or address changes, by the embedding the proposal chose (the renderer mounted with {view, item, embedded: true} and its own state object, or the ?pane=1 frame). A click on a part goes to /diagram with that part selected. Nothing loads (no ELK, no libavoid) until the section opens; the item page's poll does not re-lay the diagram unless the path changed; closing and reopening leaks no listeners or timers (the page guard of diagram-lines-stay-attached).
Definition of done:
1. On the roadmap demo /item/ticket%2F<done ticket> opening 'Draw its path' shows an svg with the stocks todo and in-progress and the valve started; switching to Blocks shows the developer's block and its loop whole.
2. With the section closed no request for elk.bundled.js is made and the item page's load time is unchanged (measured before and after).
3. No console error; the Diagram page's render tests and page-polling tests pass.
Files: ergostat/web/static/diagram.js, dynamics.js, blocks.js, interact.js (state scoping), pages.js, style.css, tests/test_items_page.py.
Acceptance tests: the browser checks above. If mounting needs more than the budget because of global state, stop and file a proposal splitting the renderer's state first.
Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: agent-page-narrow-ai-and-decision
gaps.title: The Agent page shows a narrow AI's specification and a decision agent's means, as the proposal settles
gaps.definition:
Problem: after agent-show-page the person, ai, program and rule rungs show how they work; narrow-ai and decision show only their contract and observed decisions, because nothing declares a specification or a set of answers (ergostat/spec/compile.py:83, KIND_RUNS :114), and no demo has either rung.
Change: implement what docs/proposals/agent-means.md settles: the declared key(s), if any, in spec/compile.py TYPE_KEYS with a check; the 'Its specification' section for narrow-ai and 'How it decides' for decision in static/agent.js (declared answers each with its count in the window from state.decisions, an answer outside them flagged, an answer never given shown as such); the ladder move shown as the same block's history; the demo or fixture agents the proposal names.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal's acceptance points hold on the named demo or fixture.
2. /agent/NAME for its narrow-ai agent shows its prompt rendered and its specification rows.
3. /agent/NAME for its decision agent shows its declared answers (if the proposal declares them) with counts, and an undeclared answer flagged.
4. `ergostat check` reports a decision line outside the declared answers (if declared).
5. SPEC and docs/vocabulary.md updated as the proposal lists.
Files: as the proposal lists; expected ergostat/spec/compile.py, ergostat/state.py, ergostat/web/agent_spec.py, ergostat/web/static/agent.js, docs/SPEC.md, one demo, tests.
Acceptance tests: a compile test for the key; an API test for the tally against declared answers; a browser test on the named demo.
Budget: 200 net lines; revise to the proposal's figure.

gaps.name: control-aware-completion-estimates
gaps.title: The completion estimates run the blocks' gates and the stocks they read, as the proposal defines
gaps.definition:
Problem: ergostat/numbers/eta.py keeps each block's capacity fixed for the whole horizon and ignores the gates that start the blocks and the stocks they read; on the factory those set throughput (pool 36, 1 building, 97 ready while machine-full = 1). eta-refused-takes-are-a-closed-gate approximates this with a measured concurrency cap; the owner asked for the control model and the system dynamics model in the simulation.
Change: build what docs/proposals/control-aware-estimates.md settles, split into the gaps it names if it says so. The outcome the owner sees: on the factory the Timeline's projected gaps start as the gates would admit them (a handful at once while machine-full holds, more as headroom returns), in the dispatcher's order, each with p50, p90 and a why naming what keeps it waiting ('implement-when closed: machine-full'); the Lanes show a gate's closed spans; the legend's 'last gap done' is a clock time (filed Q34's format) the backtest shows calibrated. Where a gate is evaluated it supersedes the measured-concurrency cap, through the one capacity function. numbers/closedloop.py gains an entry for stepping gates on simulated counts; an input kept at its reading is said in the why.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal's backtest bar is met on the factory snapshot (p90 coverage at least 0.8 on its cuts) and on the gated fixture record in CI, and the four existing records do not regress beyond their spread.
2. The estimates are worked out within their budget on the factory record (at least 20 runs), off the web server's request path.
3. SPEC §5a Completion estimates is rewritten to match; the Timeline's 'Not modelled' note is updated.
4. The Lanes show a gate's closed spans.
Files: ergostat/numbers/eta.py, etamodel.py, closedloop.py, ergostat/web/eta_api.py, ergostat/web/static/relations.js, tests/test_eta.py, tests/eta_backtest.py, docs/SPEC.md.
Acceptance tests: as the proposal names them, at least test_eta::test_a_gate_on_an_item_count_closes_the_block, ::test_a_kept_input_is_said_in_the_why, ::test_gated_fixture_backtest_meets_the_bar.
Budget: set by the proposal; not over 400 net lines without the Coordinator's raise.

gaps.name: stories-rerun-after-owner-list
gaps.title: The stories are walked again on the demos after the owner's list and the first redesign pieces, and each is recorded as possible and obvious or not
gaps.owner_items: All (the measure of the owner's objective: a newcomer can do it)
gaps.definition:
Problem: every acceptance in this plan is a DOM, timing or count assertion. None measures the objective the design review measured: of 46 stories, 18 were impossible and none was both possible and obvious. Without walking the stories again nobody knows whether the Goals rename, the Items page, the legend-first panel and the box rows moved that number, or whether two gaps that each pass their tests left a story worse (the hidden-finished search of F1, the count mismatch of F4, requests pushed below the legend in E1).
Change: walk every story of docs/roadmap/stories.md on the demos and fixtures it names, with a browser, as a reader who has not seen the code: for each, the steps taken, a screenshot of the answer, and a verdict (impossible / possible / possible and obvious by the story's own bound), in docs/roadmap/stories-results/<date>.md with the baseline beside it. Stories whose surface is not built yet are marked 'not yet'. For each story that is not 'possible and obvious' and that an already merged gap was meant to serve, request one quick gap naming the story, the step that failed and the screenshot (through the Coordinator, with this gap as parent). No product code here.
Definition of done:
1. The results file has a row per story with verdict, steps and a screenshot name, and the baseline verdict beside it.
2. Stories A2, A3, B1, B2, E1, F1, F4 and the new F6-F8 each have a verdict (not 'not yet') if the gaps this depends on have landed.
3. Every regression against the baseline has a requested gap.
4. A summary line: how many impossible, possible, possible and obvious, against 18 / 28 / 0.
Files: docs/roadmap/stories-results/<date>.md, screenshots beside it.
Acceptance tests: review: every story has a row; every 'impossible' has a requested gap or a named waiting gap of this plan.
Budget: documentation only. For the Coordinator: request the same walk (same definition) at the end of each later user-facing milestone; stories-rerun-after-redesigns is the last.

gaps.name: flows-only-chain-layout-pilot
gaps.title: Pilot: Flows only with one row per chain, upstream first, measured against the current engine for the layout decision
gaps.owner_items: 10 (the flow of an item clear and obvious; pilot for 'maybe worth rewriting entirely')
gaps.definition:
Problem: flows-only-arranges-the-flows lays the flows out alone with the current engine (ELK layered plus the repair passes), which makes the drawing smaller but does not promise what the owner asked for: 'the flow of an item clear and obvious', each chain of stocks read left to right as one row. Whether that needs a small layout of our own is also the cheapest real evidence for the question 'is the layout worth rewriting' (diagram-layout-engine-proposal), because the flows subgraph is the simplest case a domain layout must get right.
Change: a small chain layout for the Flows-only subgraph in a new ergostat/web/static/chains.js (about 150 lines): rows from the pipe graph, each chain of stocks joined by pipes one row, upstream first; cloud inflows before or above, drains below, rework in a lane under its row; chains stacked by system in feeding order; pipes orthogonal with at most one bend between neighbours; routing through the existing router. It is used for Flows only when it meets the rules below on a graph, and the current engine's result otherwise (the choice recorded in S.layoutRuns). The measurements against the current engine on the corpus (rule counts, area, time to attached and tidy on the six demos and the factory graph fixture) are written into a section of docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md (created here if not yet there) as the pilot's evidence.
Definition of done:
1. With Flows only on, on image-squeeze lab, ticket-factory open=* and the-job open=*, every chain of two or more stocks lies on one row with the source left of the target for at least 90% of pipes, rework excepted; layout rules 1 and 4 have 0 instances.
2. Area at most 70% of the full view and no worse than the current engine's Flows-only area on the corpus median.
3. Toggling Flows only twice still returns the full view unchanged; pins per mode still hold.
4. The comparison table is in the proposal file, produced by a command it names.
Files: new ergostat/web/static/chains.js, diagram.js (the choice), layouts.js, index.html, tests/layout_corpus.py (a flows-only view and the comparison), tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md (pilot section).
Acceptance tests: test_flows_only_rows on the three demos; the corpus comparison command.
Budget: 170 net lines of JS plus 50 of tests.

gaps.name: diagram-layout-engine-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: keep ELK plus correcting passes, or a layout of our own for Dynamics, decided with measurements (docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the owner asks whether the layout is worth rewriting entirely. Today a drawing is made by ELK layered with the anchors-wrap preset (ergostat/web/static/layouts.js), then about fifteen passes that move parts or lines to repair it (placeSatellites, packLoose, port-turn re-layouts, restack/routeCuts, anchorLayout, seatCloudFlows, centreValves, the comparison layout, applyPins, orientValves: diagram.js:74-232), then libavoid in a worker (avoid.js) and six page passes (straighten, untangle, uncross, sdSeparate, sdAroundSatellites, unjog): about 3,800 lines across diagram.js, avoid.js, layouts.js, places.js, satellites.js, valves.js, untangle.js, routeparts.js, interact.js, plus 12 ?layout= presets readers never need. Parts are placed by one pass and lines by another, which is where owner items 5 and 7 came from. The verdict today is 'not warranted yet': the slowness is one router parameter plus repeated ELK runs, fixed by the gaps this depends on. This proposal decides what is left, with numbers taken after them, and with the chain-layout pilot's measured comparison as its first evidence.
Change: complete docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md (the pilot wrote its section). It decides:
(a) Dynamics: extend the chain arrangement into a domain layout (chains of one conserved quantity as rows, upstream first; clouds beside their valves; auxiliaries and goals beside what they drive; connectors as arcs, as Vensim and Stella draw them) replacing ELK and the repair passes, or keep ELK with the passes made into one geometry owner (each pass declares what it moves and invalidates its lines).
(b) Blocks: whether ELK layered stays, with one loop per row (R4 piece 6).
(c) Stability: new parts placed without moving existing ones; opening one system leaves the others in place (R8 piece 5); positions stable across polls as the factory's structure grows.
(d) Budgets per view and size (time to attached and to tidy at 100, 300 and 1,000 shapes) on the demos, the factory graph fixture and scripts/scale_model at N=10 and 30.
(e) Large views: route only what is on screen, or draw closed boxes until opened (docs/proposals/scale.md #13); where routing runs and whether libavoid stays.
(f) How bundled connectors (owner item 6), corner frames (item 8) and boxes with goal rows (R1) fit the chosen engine.
(g) Whether the ?layout= presets survive (default: removed from the page, kept for the corpus via --engine).
(h) A staged plan: confirm or amend open-leaves-other-systems-in-place, dynamics-chains-upstream-short-pipes and dynamics-trunk-bundling-in-open-systems, each with layout-rule counts and a timing budget, and what is deleted at each stage.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal exists with measured tables (corpus rule counts and times per option) collected by a script committed beside the corpus and run offline on the fixtures.
2. A prototype of option (a) beyond Flows only draws ticket-factory, image-squeeze and the factory graph fixture, in a branch only.
3. A recommendation of rewrite, partial or keep, naming what is deleted.
4. The owner is sent the one-sentence decision it asks for (only if the recommendation is to rewrite or delete; 'keep' needs no answer).
Files: docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md, a measurement script under tests/ or scripts/, an optional prototype branch.
Acceptance tests: the script prints the table the proposal quotes; the factory's proposal review passes.
Budget: the proposal (300-500 lines) plus a script of about 150 lines; no product code merged.

gaps.name: perf-page-server-process-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: the page server stops sharing the engine's Python process (docs/proposals/page-server-process.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem: `ergostat run` starts the page server and the engine in one Python process (ergostat/cli/running.py:117-126): on the factory 266 sensors, 37 machine blocks, 57-96 threads and every web answer share one GIL. The process ran at 114-165% CPU and a native sample of the wedged process showed most threads waiting for the GIL (CPU in zlib inflate_fast re-decompressing event blocks, segments.py:421). Even after the snapshot and queue fixes every page answer competes with the engine's pass, and a heavy page (Model's fit: 55 s live against 7 s on an idle copy) slows the engine. The per-goal background work (performance words, forecasts) adds to the same process. This is docs/proposals/scale.md #15, never measured on the real factory. It is decided with numbers taken after the two gaps it depends on.
Change: a proposal only. It compares, measured on a copy of the factory state and on the factory-size fixture under a replayed load: (a) the page server as its own process, started and stopped by the runner, reading the same stores read-only; (b) the engine publishing its snapshot each tick (a file or the engine socket) with the page only serialising it; (c) no change, if the p95 after the other gaps meets the web-answers-fast goal. It covers: what in Live and the APIs depends on being in the engine's process (running_pid, Live.reloaded after an accept, history.note, the identify-laws thread, record_fits, crash reports, remote mTLS, push intake /api/events and /api/hooks/); where the per-goal background cache runs; how the owner's POSTs reach the engine (engine.sock) and stay the only writes; the record's multi-process guarantees (segments head + flock, the item index, SQLite WAL readers); memory (RSS 1.6 GB fresh, 2.4 GB after 4 h: does a second process double the caches); the tunnel, restarts and the drain switch; the measurement plan and target (p50/p95 of every page's answers and the engine's pass time before and after).
Definition of done:
1. docs/proposals/page-server-process.md answers every point with measured numbers per option and one recommendation.
2. It links scale.md.
3. It ends with the implementation gaps to file, sized and ordered, or says none are needed.
Files: docs/proposals/page-server-process.md; a throwaway benchmark script under dev/.
Acceptance tests: review; the numbers are reproducible by a named command.
Budget: the proposal; no product code.

gaps.name: dynamics-trunk-bundling-in-open-systems
gaps.title: Bundled connectors inside and between open systems: one trunk into a part fed from far away, routed along frames
gaps.definition:
Problem: dynamics-module-bundled-connectors bundles only lines between two closed modules. With systems open, many connectors between two systems or into one part from far away still cross each other and stack their signs: on :8796 ?system=product five or six connectors converge on churn and four on regressions (shots/plan-notation-sf-product-dyn.png); long connectors leaving an opened system run across the drawing instead of along its frame (R8 piece 8). This needs edge bundling in the router (ergostat/web/static/avoid.js), so it waits for the layout decision; it reuses the 'bundle' edge kind, its members and its panel that dynamics-module-bundled-connectors built (no second representation); and it relies on the stand-in/attached-line machinery so a dragged trunk never points at an old place.
Change: build what docs/proposals/dynamics-bundled-connectors.md settled for open systems, on the engine docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md chose, and no more: bundle detection by (source system, target system) and by fan-in or fan-out above the proposal's thresholds, producing the same 'bundle' edges with members; one routed path per trunk with branches routed to its ends, trunks leaving an opened system routed along its frame; the trunk in the connector tone at the proposal's weight with its mark; each branch keeps its own head and sign on its unshared segment (filed Q25's rule per branch). Hovering a branch traces one link; the trunk's panel (the module bundle's panel) lists its links; loop tracing lights trunk and branches; Flows only filters members; a drag re-routes the trunk; correspondence rings, keyboard, legend and export include it. Detectors in tests/layout_rules.py: bundle-sign (every member's sign lies on its own branch) and bundle-split (no split point inside a part).
Definition of done:
1. On :8796/ with product and factory open the product-factory connectors are drawn as at most two trunks, each with a mark equal to its members.
2. Every member link has its own arrowhead and sign, nearest to its own branch.
3. Corpus counts meet the numbers the proposal set: crossings down, no rise in sign collisions, marker failures or line-through-part; line-detached stays 0 after a scripted drag.
4. Flows only, export (PNG and SVG), dark mode and correspondence colours render a trunk correctly.
5. docs/layout-rules.md gains the bundling rule in measured form; DESIGN.md's Dynamics notation names it.
Files: ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, avoid.js, routeparts.js, diagram.js (redrawLine), colours.js, export.js, style.css, tests/layout_rules.py, tests/layout_geometry.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md, docs/DESIGN.md; possibly ergostat/dynamics.py.
Acceptance tests: on :8796/, :8796 ?system=product and :8797/ everything open: trunk and member counts match the graph; no bundle-split violation; after a drag every trunk end lies on its part's boundary.
Budget: 350 net lines, refined by the proposal.

gaps.name: blocks-textbook-levels-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: Blocks above the leaf: classified subsystems, a top level with references and summing junctions, rows per loop (docs/proposals/blocks-levels.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4): at the leaf the notation is right (summing junctions, r/e/u/y/d, H on the return, C(z) with sampler and hold). Above the leaf it is not a block diagram: the top level is opaque 'Q' boxes, seven in a column with no signals on big, two unconnected on the-job, one unlabelled wire on ticket-factory; no reference, no summing junction; Q is undefined (it reads to a control engineer as the Youla parameter) and changes to P with different dimensions when opened (shots/story-6-g6-blocks-top.png, ceb-annotated-sf-top.png, ceb-big-blocks-dark.png, story-7-h2-into-api-blocks.png). Inside, loops are not laid in signal order (story-6-g5-blocks-making.png, ceb-big-api-blocks.png). Subsystem nodes and their vectors are built in ergostat/blockdiagram.py (:1325-1341, :1423) and drawn in blocks.js.
Change: write docs/proposals/blocks-levels.md settling: (1) classification of a subsystem as C (it holds controllers acting on another system's process), P (it is acted on) or a named block when mixed, with the same letter and p x m at both levels (the disturbance counted at both); Q dropped; (2) the top level's form: references and a summing junction ahead of the controlling subsystem, labelled signals between systems, H on the return (acceptance: story G6 on software-factory); (3) uncoupled systems as parallel rows each with its own r and y and the caption 'no signals between these' (big, the-job), built on the same top-level assembly as (2), after it; (4) the row layout inside a system: one loop per row in signal order, upstream first, couplings downward, the sensor under its own process (acceptance: story G5 on ticket-factory making and the chain on big api), and whether ELK layered can do it with constraints (with diagram-layout-engine-proposal); (5) how the closed block's r/y and status (blocks-closed-block-r-y-and-status) sit on the classified block's ports. It confirms or amends the four build gaps.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal settles 1-5 with a sketch for :8796 top level, :8797 top level and ticket-factory making.
2. A control engineer's textbook reference is cited for each form.
3. It lists the tests each build gap must add.
Files: docs/proposals/blocks-levels.md, docs/DISCIPLINES.md (link).
Acceptance tests: review only.
Budget: about 200 lines, no code.

gaps.name: blocks-subsystems-classified-c-p
gaps.title: Blocks: subsystems are classified C, P or a named block, with the same letter and dimensions at both levels
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 3): every closed subsystem is 'Q_name p x m'; Q is undefined in the legend and becomes P with different dimensions when opened, because the disturbance is counted at one level and not the other (shots/story-7-h1-blocks.png, story-7-h2-into-api-blocks.png, ce-sf-blocks-factory.png).
Change, as the proposal settles: ergostat/blockdiagram.py classifies each subsystem node from what it holds (controllers acting on another system's process: C; processes acted on from outside: P; both or neither: its own name as a named block) and counts inputs and outputs, disturbances included, the same way at the level above and inside; the node carries {letter, p, m} and its ports in a stated order (references, outputs, disturbances) that later gaps print on. blocks.js draws the letter with the system's name as subscript and p x m; the legend (filed Q68) defines the letter and p x m. Q is removed everywhere.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796, :8797 and :8791 no block is labelled Q.
2. For every subsystem the letter and p x m printed on the closed block equal those in the frame title when opened (a test walks every system of every demo).
3. The legend defines C, P and p x m.
4. Render tests pass.
Files: ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, tests (a blockdiagram unit test of classification on a small spec; tests/test_diagram_rendering.py).
Acceptance tests: unit: a system holding only controllers is C, only processes P, mixed named; the both-levels walk on the six demos.
Budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-closed-block-r-y-and-status
gaps.title: Blocks: a closed system's block prints r and y on its ports and its status in words under it
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1 piece 5): in Blocks a closed system is 'Q_service 3x3' and nothing else (shots/story-1-b1-blocks.png, story-7-h1-blocks.png, pmb-img-blocks-closed.png): no reference, no output value, nothing marked off, so story H1 failed. Blocks must stay monochrome (decision 2), so status is text, never colour. The ports to print on are those of the classified block (blocks-subsystems-classified-c-p: its letter, p x m and port order).
Change, as the proposal settles: the closed subsystem block (ergostat/blockdiagram.py subsystem nodes; drawn in ergostat/web/static/blocks.js) keeps its symbol and dimensions and prints on its ports each reference r with its value and each output y with its value (as port labels, up to the proposal's limit, then 'N more'), and one status line under the block made from the goals' words (goalWord): '3 control loops, 1 off' with the off loop's e in bold with its value; neutral words (approaching, in grace) are counted in regular weight when they exist. A click on a port label opens that goal's evidence. Values come with the Blocks graph answer and update with the poll.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture with an off loop, in ?view=blocks top level the block holding it says 'N control loops, 1 off' and shows that loop's r and y values.
