2. No colour distinguishes off: the computed stroke and fill of an off block equal a holding one's; the difference is text and weight.
3. The numbers equal /api/loops for the same goals at the same moment; the words equal their `word`.
4. The Blocks legend explains the status line; render tests pass.
Files: ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, style.css, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, a blockdiagram unit test.
Acceptance tests: unit: a closed subsystem node carries r/y rows and the off count; browser: the status line text and the monochrome check on the fixture and on :8797.
Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-top-level-reference-and-sum
gaps.title: Blocks top level: references and a summing junction ahead of the controlling subsystem, labelled signals, H on the return
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 4): the Blocks top level shows subsystem boxes joined by an unlabelled wire, with no reference, no summing junction and no return path, so it does not read as a control loop (shots/story-6-g6-blocks-top.png, ceb-annotated-sf-top.png). Story G6 on software-factory failed. Needs the C/P classification to know which subsystem controls which.
Change, as the proposal settles: when a C subsystem's controllers act on a P subsystem's processes, the level above draws the loop between them in textbook form: the references r (a vector when several, with count) entering a summing junction ahead of C, the error e into C, the command u from C to P labelled, the output y leaving P, and the return through H (the sensing vector) to the junction's minus input. Signals between systems are labelled with their names or 'k signals' as vectors. The disturbance d enters P. Built in ergostat/blockdiagram.py's top-level assembly (:1325-1341), which this gap restructures into one function taking groups of systems (coupled groups here; blocks-uncoupled-systems-parallel-rows adds the uncoupled group to the same function), drawn with the existing glyphs in blocks.js.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 ?view=blocks top level a summing junction precedes the controlling subsystem, with r, e, u, y labelled and H on the return (story G6 passes).
2. Every wire at the top level has a label.
3. Opening either subsystem shows the same signals at its frame's ports.
4. Layout rules report no new critical violation on the six demos.
Files: ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, a blockdiagram unit test.
Acceptance tests: unit: a two-system spec yields junction, r, e, u, y and an H return at the top level; browser: story G6 on :8796.
Budget: 160 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-uncoupled-systems-parallel-rows
gaps.title: Blocks: uncoupled systems are parallel rows with their own r and y and a caption saying no signals join them
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 5): on big the Blocks top level is seven boxes in a column with no signals, on the-job two unconnected boxes (shots/ceb-big-blocks-dark.png, sreb-job-blocks-fit.png); a reader cannot tell whether signals are missing or there are none. The top-level assembly (ergostat/blockdiagram.py:1325-1341) is restructured by blocks-top-level-reference-and-sum into one function over groups of systems; this gap adds the uncoupled group to it, so it follows that gap.
Change, as the proposal settles: systems with no signal between them are laid as parallel rows (a new arrangement of the top level: rows stacked, not ELK's column of boxes), each row drawn as its own loop outline with its references r entering on the left and its outputs y leaving on the right (counts as vectors), and one caption under the group: 'no signals between these systems'. Coupled systems keep the form of blocks-top-level-reference-and-sum; a model with both shows the coupled group first.
Definition of done:
1. On :8797 ?view=blocks each of the seven systems is a row with r on its left and y on its right, and the caption is present.
2. On :8792 the two systems are two rows with the caption.
3. On :8796 (coupled) the caption is absent.
4. Rows are ordered as the systems are in Dynamics; text at least 11 px.
Files: ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, layouts.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: browser checks 1-3; a unit test that an uncoupled spec yields rows with r/y ports.
Budget: 100 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-one-loop-per-row
gaps.title: Blocks inside a system: one loop per row in signal order, upstream first, the sensor under its own process
gaps.owner_items: R4 piece 6 (with R8 piece 7 for Blocks)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 6): inside a system the loops are placed by ELK's layering with no regard for signal order: on ticket-factory making and on big api the chain of loops is drawn downstream-first in places and sensors sit far from their processes (shots/story-6-g5-blocks-making.png, ceb-big-api-blocks.png, story-7-h2-into-api-blocks.png). Story G5 failed.
Change, as the proposal settles: within a system frame each control loop is one row read left to right (junction, C, actuator, P, y), its sensor H under its own process on the return; rows are ordered upstream first by the processes' material order (the Dynamics chain order), and couplings between loops run downward. Implemented as constraints on the ELK layered layout in blocks.js / layouts.js (partitioning and model order), or as the proposal chose. A cascade's inner loop sits inside its outer loop's row. Add a layout rule 'loop-row-order' to tests/layout_rules.py and docs/layout-rules.md.
Definition of done:
1. On :8791 ?view=blocks&system=making every loop's blocks lie on one row in signal order and rows follow the chain's order (story G5 passes).
2. On :8797 api the chain q1..qN is top to bottom upstream first.
3. Every sensor's x-range overlaps its process's.
4. The rule reports 0 violations on the six demos; no rise in critical counts in the corpus.
Files: ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, layouts.js, ergostat/blockdiagram.py (row order hints), tests/layout_rules.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md.
Acceptance tests: the new rule over the demos; browser checks on :8791 making and :8797 api.
Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-crossings-hop-dot-slash
gaps.title: Blocks: a hop at a crossing, a dot only at a take-off, the vector slash away from crossings
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 9): in Blocks two wires that cross are drawn as a plain cross, the same mark a junction without its dot would make; take-off dots are sometimes drawn where wires merely cross; and a vector's slash and count can land on a crossing (shots/ceb-is-service-fit.png, ce-sf-blocks-product.png). A control engineer cannot tell a connection from a crossing.
Change: after routing, blocks.js computes the crossings of drawn wire segments (segments are orthogonal, so the test is cheap) and draws a small semicircular hop on the horizontal wire at each crossing; a filled dot is drawn only where a wire takes off from another (a shared end point on a segment's interior in the graph, not geometry); the vector slash and its count (blocks.js:932-950) are placed on the longest crossing-free stretch of the wire, at least 12 px from any crossing or bend. Add layout rules 'crossing-without-hop', 'dot-not-at-takeoff' and 'slash-on-crossing' to tests/layout_rules.py. Export keeps the hops.
Definition of done:
1. On :8793, :8796 and :8797 in Blocks with everything open, every wire crossing has a hop and no dot.
2. Every dot is at a take-off in the graph.
3. No vector slash lies within 12 px of a crossing.
4. The three rules report 0 on the six demos; redraw after a drag keeps them.
Files: ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, export.js, tests/layout_rules.py, tests/layout_geometry.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md.
Acceptance tests: the three rules over the corpus; a drag-then-check browser test.
Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: blocks-model-health-on-the-blocks
gaps.title: Blocks: model health is printed on the blocks, from the same source as the evidence panel
gaps.definition:
Problem (R4 piece 10): whether a process is identified, whether a stock's balance closes and whether an actuator's commands move anything are in the evidence and loop panels only; on the drawing every P looks equally trustworthy (shots/ceb-is-ctrl-panel.png 'Its process is not identified yet', story-2-c2-evidence-off.png 'never opened' beside 'Moves 1.62/h').
Change: under a process block P a muted line 'not identified' or 'balance off by 30.5' (with unit and window) when the snapshot's residual is significant; under an actuator 'commanded 18x, moved 0' when commands in the window produced no movement. The words and numbers come from the one function the evidence panel's actor line uses (filed Q28) and the loop-control summary (no request per block: the Blocks graph answer carries them from the snapshot and the cached loop summary). Monochrome; a legend row each; a click opens the evidence at that line.
Definition of done:
1. On :8793 ?view=blocks a process without an identified model reads 'not identified' under P.
2. On a fixture where an actuator was commanded and nothing moved, the line reads 'commanded N x, moved 0' and equals the evidence panel's line.
3. A process whose balance closes and is identified prints nothing.
4. No extra request per block on load.
Files: ergostat/blockdiagram.py, ergostat/web/server.py (graph answer), ergostat/web/static/blocks.js, details.js (shared words), tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, a unit test.
Acceptance tests: unit: node health fields from a snapshot fixture; browser: 1-3.
Budget: 110 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-goals-and-loop-folding-proposal
gaps.title: Proposal: every goal drawn in Dynamics, and which feedback loops are drawn, named or folded (docs/proposals/dynamics-goals-and-loops.md)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5): the leaf notation is Sterman's and stays. But on software-factory's product, the demo's subject, none of its three goals is drawn (image-squeeze and big do draw 'desired' and 'gap': shots/sdxb-8797-api.png); all 18 elementary loops are drawn with path names ('all-live via regressions and churn and asks'), their markers and names piled on each other and on the users stock; '+1' on a marker is unexplained (story-6-g3-dyn-product.png, sdxb-annotated-product.png, story-6-g4-R2.png). Which goals get a desired level and gap, and which loops are worth drawing, are modelling decisions with layout cost.
Change: write docs/proposals/dynamics-goals-and-loops.md settling: (1) the rule by which every goal is drawn as a goal-seeking structure in its own system (desired level, gap, the link to the flow it drives, or the 'no feedback' mark when nothing closes it), why product's goals are not drawn today (ergostat/dynamics.py) and the port link when the actor is in another system; (2) which loops are drawn: named loops and one per goal; the rest listed as minor in the side list and drawn when selected; '+1' removed; the ranking (dominance now, /api/dominance) and the cap; (3) loop names: a `loops:` entry may name a loop in the model (SPEC §12a); the diagram shows the name, the panel the path; the names for software-factory product's loops; (4) what the loop count on a box and in the list then means (with filed Q22 and the heading of goals-and-loops-cross-referenced); (5) the layout cost of the added gap structures on :8797. It confirms or amends dynamics-every-goal-drawn and dynamics-minor-loops-folded-and-named.
Definition of done:
1. The proposal settles 1-5 with a before/after sketch of software-factory product.
2. Each rule cites Sterman's form.
3. The acceptance for each build gap is stated as counts on the demos' structure.
Files: docs/proposals/dynamics-goals-and-loops.md.
Acceptance tests: review only.
Budget: about 180 lines, no code.

gaps.name: dynamics-every-goal-drawn
gaps.title: Dynamics: every goal is drawn as desired level and gap in its own system
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5 piece 3): on :8796 ?system=product none of the three goals is drawn, while the users stock's panel names a goal on it: the diagram and the panel disagree (shots/story-6-g3-dyn-product.png, sdxb-8796-product.png). image-squeeze and big draw 'desired' and 'gap' correctly (sdxb-8797-api.png). Decision 2: in Dynamics a goal is a goal-seeking auxiliary.
Change, as the proposal settles: ergostat/dynamics.py emits for every goal, in the goal's own system, the desired-level auxiliary, the gap auxiliary and the connector from the gap to the flow its actor drives; when the actor's flow is in another system the link goes through the system's port; when nothing closes the goal (open loop, no actor) the gap carries a 'no feedback' mark and no link. Bounds are written as filed Q23. The stock's panel and the drawing use the same goal list. The legend and the Guide frame that shows a goal-seeking structure explain 'no feedback'.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 ?system=product the three goals are drawn, each with desired level, gap and its link or the 'no feedback' mark.
2. For every demo, every goal in /api/loops has a gap node in /api/graph?view=dynamics&open=* (a test walks them).
3. The users panel and the diagram name the same goals.
4. Layout rules report no new critical violation; the legend explains 'no feedback'.
Files: ergostat/dynamics.py, ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, ergostat/guide.py, tests/test_dynamics_view.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: unit: a goal with an actor in another system yields gap, desired and a port link; an open-loop goal yields the mark; the every-goal walk over the demos.
Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-minor-loops-folded-and-named
gaps.title: Dynamics draws the named loops and one per goal; minor loops are listed and drawn when selected; a loop may be named in the model
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5 pieces 4 and 5): on software-factory product all 18 elementary loops are drawn, named by their paths ('all-live via regressions and churn and asks'), markers and names piled on each other and on the users stock; '+1' on a marker is unexplained (shots/story-6-g4-R2.png, story-6-g4-B1.png, sdxb-annotated-product.png). A reader cannot find the two or three mechanisms that explain the system.
Change, as the proposal settles: (1) the drawing shows a marker only for loops named in the model and one loop per goal (the balancing loop through its gap); every other loop is 'minor': listed in the side list's folded 'minor loops (N)' and drawn (marker and lit path, in the accent as any trace) only while selected or hovered there. '+1' is removed. (2) a `loops:` entry in the model may name a loop by its parts (SPEC §12a); the diagram prints the name at the marker, the panel shows the path; an unnamed drawn loop is 'B3' with its goal's name. (3) the software-factory demo names product's main loops (e.g. 'word of mouth', 'support load'). (4) the loop that dominates now (/api/dominance) is named at the head of the list (R5 piece 8's second half).
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 ?system=product at most the named loops plus one per goal have markers (count asserted against the model), and no marker text contains '+'.
2. Selecting a minor loop in the list draws its marker and path; deselecting removes it.
3. A named loop shows its name on the diagram and its path in the panel.
4. The box's and list's loop counts agree (filed Q22) and say 'N named, M minor'.
Files: ergostat/dynamics.py, ergostat/spec/causal.py (names), ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, demos/software-factory (loop names), docs/SPEC.md §12a, tests/test_dynamics_view.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: unit: naming and the minor flag; browser: 1-3 on :8796.
Budget: 150 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-marker-collision-pass
gaps.title: Dynamics: loop markers sit at the centre of their loop, and markers, names and signs never overlap parts, pipes or each other
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5 piece 6): loop markers and their names are placed without regard to what is under them: on software-factory product they pile on each other and on the users stock, and polarity signs overlap pipes (shots/story-6-g3-crop.png, story-1-dark-product.png, story-1-b6-zoom.png). No layout rule measures it.
Change: in ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js the marker of a loop is placed at the centroid of its loop's polygon (the drawn parts in loop order); then one collision pass moves markers, loop names and polarity signs (signs only along their own arrow, per filed Q25) off parts, pipes, connectors and each other by the smallest shift, keeping a marker inside its polygon when possible; a marker that cannot be placed is dropped from the drawing and stays in the list. The pass runs after routing and after a drag. Add layout rules 'marker-on-part', 'marker-overlap' and 'sign-on-pipe' to tests/layout_rules.py and docs/layout-rules.md, measured on the drawn SVG.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 ?system=product and :8793 open=* the three rules report 0.
2. Every drawn marker lies inside its loop's polygon or within 20 px of its edge.
3. The layout corpus (--generated 300) reports the new rules with no rise in other critical counts.
4. The pass costs under 30 ms on :8797 open=*.
Files: ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, tests/layout_rules.py, tests/layout_geometry.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md.
Acceptance tests: the rules over the demos and the corpus; a drag-then-check test.
Budget: 130 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-doubt-on-flows-and-processes
gaps.title: Dynamics: doubt about a flow or a process is drawn on it
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5 piece 7): filed Q35 draws doubt about a stock on the stock. A flow whose fitted rate explains nothing and a process that is not identified look as certain as any other part; the doubt is in the Model page's tables only (shots/newcomer-briefed-is-service.png, story-2-c6-modelling.png).
Change: a valve whose flow's fit is worse than its mean (the fit table's verdict, numbers/review) is drawn hatched with the muted caption 'fits worse than its mean'; a part whose process is not identified carries a '?' after its name; both come with the Dynamics graph answer from the cached fit (no request per part) and are the same marks in every demo. One line each in 'How to read it' (drawn-when rows) and in the Guide frame that explains a flow. A click opens the part's panel at the fit line. The marks are tone and pattern, not a new colour.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture with a flow fitted worse than its mean the valve has the hatch pattern and the caption; a well-fitted flow has neither.
2. On :8793 a part with no identified process shows '?', equal to the Model page's 'not identified' list.
3. The legend rows appear only when the marks are drawn.
4. Light and dark; export keeps the hatch.
Files: ergostat/dynamics.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, style.css, export.js, ergostat/guide.py, tests/test_dynamics_view.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: unit: node doubt fields from a fit fixture; browser: 1-3.
Budget: 100 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-off-status-on-the-part
gaps.title: Dynamics: a goal's gap prints the goal's one word, and an off goal's gap and loop marker take the off colour, never the accent
gaps.definition:
Problem (R5 piece 8): in Dynamics nothing on the drawing says which goal is off; the reader matches names from the side list to parts. Once every goal's gap is drawn (dynamics-every-goal-drawn) the gap is the place to say it. The accent already means selection and trace (docs/DESIGN.md's colour rules, settled in diagram-line-tones), so an off goal must not use it, or a traced loop and an off goal would be the same colour.
Change: the gap auxiliary of a goal that is not holding prints the goal's `word` through goalWord (goal-row-one-renderer; no mapping of status in dynamics.js): 'off' with how far ('off by 36', the one phrase of one-phrase-for-how-far-off when present) in --bad, the marker of the goal's balancing loop in --bad too; 'no feedback' for an open goal; the neutral words (approaching, in grace) in the neutral token when they exist; holding goals stay in ink with no word. Not colour alone: the word is always printed. The gap -> flow link stays full ink. Values update with the values poll without a re-layout. The legend and the Guide frame explain the mark.
Definition of done:
1. On a fixture with off and holding goals, open=*: each off goal's gap node has the 'off' text and computes to --bad; holding goals' gaps do not.
2. The word on each gap equals that goal's `word` in /api/loops.
3. A lit (selected) loop's stroke and an off gap's stroke compute to different colours, in both themes.
4. A goal turning off between polls is marked without a re-layout (layout counter unchanged).
Files: ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, style.css, ergostat/guide.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: a browser test for 1-4 on the fixture.
Budget: 40 net lines.

gaps.name: dynamics-chains-upstream-short-pipes
gaps.title: Dynamics: chains are drawn upstream first from the top left, clouds beside their valve, pipes with one bend at most
gaps.definition:
Problem: in the full Dynamics view a chain of queues is drawn downstream-first in places (big api; the-job incidents: shots/story-7-h2-thejob-incidents.png, story-7-h2-open-api.png) and pipes take long detours with clouds far from their valves (big's q2 -> q3), against the owner's layout rules 1, 4 and 5 (docs/layout-rules.md). flows-only-chain-layout-pilot does this for the Flows-only view; the full view waits for the engine decision so the work is not thrown away.
Change, on the engine docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md chose: in the full Dynamics layout each chain of stocks joined by pipes is a row read left to right, upstream first, the first chain at the top left; a cloud sits beside its valve (within one valve width); a pipe between neighbours in a chain has at most one bend; auxiliaries and gaps are placed beside what they drive without displacing the row. Enforced by layout rules 1, 4, 5 and 10 as critical in tests/layout_rules.py for the full view, with the counts the proposal set.
Definition of done:
1. On :8797 ?system=api and :8792 incidents every chain's stocks are ordered left to right in flow order (source left of target for at least 95% of pipes, rework excepted).
2. Rules 1, 4 and 5 report 0 on the six demos; q2 -> q3 on big has at most one bend.
3. Every cloud is within one valve width of its valve.
4. Time to a tidy drawing does not exceed the proposal's budget.
Files: as the proposal lists; expected ergostat/web/static/diagram.js, layouts.js or chains.js, valves.js, tests/layout_rules.py, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md.
Acceptance tests: the rule counts over the demos and the corpus against --engine of main.
Budget: set by the proposal; not over 250 net lines.

gaps.name: diagram-text-floor-11px
gaps.title: Drawn text never falls under 11 px: the drawing pans with direction hints instead of shrinking
gaps.definition:
Problem (R8 piece 4): Fit shrinks the drawing until text is 4 to 8 px on big and software-factory (shots/story-7-h2-open-api-fit.png, ixd-big-open-all-fit.png, ceb-is-service-fit.png); in Blocks, when rows do not fit, everything is scaled down (R4 piece 8). Decision 6 says large systems matter.
Change: Fit and the fit-on-load (ergostat/web/static/diagram.js panZoom/fit) never zoom below the scale at which the smallest drawn text is 11 CSS px; when the drawing does not fit at that scale it is framed on what was asked (the opened or selected system, else the top-left chain) and the edge hints (filed Q71) say how much lies beyond and in which direction ('2 more systems to the right'). In Blocks, when a system's rows do not fit, the rows that do are shown with 'N more below'. Manual zoom-out past the floor stays possible (the reader's choice) and switches labels to the box-name level of detail. A measured check 'text-under-11px' joins the render tests on every demo and view at 1440x900 and 390x844.
Definition of done:
1. After load and after Fit on every demo and view, the smallest rendered text (getBoundingClientRect height of every text element) is at least 11 px.
2. On :8797 open=* the view is framed on the first systems with a hint naming the direction and count of the rest.
3. On :8797 ?view=blocks&system=api the rows that fit are shown with 'N more below'.
4. The check runs in tests/test_diagram_rendering.py on the six demos.
Files: ergostat/web/static/diagram.js, interact.js, blocks.js, dynamics.js, style.css, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py, docs/layout-rules.md.
Acceptance tests: the measured check; a Fit test on :8797 at both sizes.
Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: open-leaves-other-systems-in-place
gaps.title: Opening or closing one system leaves the others where they were
gaps.definition:
Problem (R8 piece 5): Open or Close of one system re-lays out the whole view, so closed boxes and other open systems move and the reader loses their place (shots/story-7-h2-open-api.png, story-0-a5-open-300ms.png); on the live factory a structural change moves what the reader was looking at. How incremental layout is done depends on the engine decision (stability is point (c) of the layout proposal).
Change, on the engine and method docs/proposals/diagram-layout-engine.md chose: opening a system lays out only its inside and grows its frame; the other top-level parts keep their relative order and are shifted only by the growth (pushed right or down), never reordered; closing shrinks it back to the box's previous place. New parts arriving on a poll are placed without moving existing ones (current places as soft pins). Hand pins are respected. Lines touching the opened system are re-routed; others keep their paths where their ends did not move.
Definition of done:
1. On :8797, opening api: every other top-level box keeps its left-to-right and top-to-bottom order, and boxes not right of or below api do not move at all.
2. Open then Close returns every part to within 2 px of where it was.
3. A part added by a poll on a fixture does not move any existing part by more than its own size.
4. Lines whose ends did not move keep their paths byte for byte.
5. Time to attached lines after Open meets the proposal's budget.
Files: as the proposal lists; expected ergostat/web/static/diagram.js, layouts.js, places.js, avoid.js, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: test_open_leaves_others_in_place on :8797 and :8796; the open-close round trip; the poll-growth fixture.
Budget: set by the proposal; not over 250 net lines.

gaps.name: diagram-roving-focus-and-arrow-keys
gaps.title: The diagram is one tab stop with roving focus; arrow keys follow pipes, connectors and signals
gaps.owner_items: R9 piece 4 (pieces 1-3 are filed Q74, Q75, Q77)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R9 piece 4): the diagram is the interface by the owner's decision, and filed Q74 makes its parts focusable. On big that is hundreds of tab stops before the side panel, and Tab order says nothing about structure (shots/a11y-8791-home.png, a11y-8797-stock-click.png). Story H5 failed.
Change: the SVG is one tab stop (roving tabindex: one part has tabindex 0, the rest -1; the last focused part is remembered per view). Arrow keys move along the structure: in Dynamics Right/Left follow the pipe downstream/upstream from a stock or valve, Up/Down step through the connectors into and out of the focused part (announcing the other end and the link's sign); in Blocks Right/Left follow the signal forward/back and Down takes the return path. On a closed box with goal rows, Down enters its rows. Enter opens the part's panel and moves focus into it; Escape returns focus to the part; I goes Into a focused system and Escape (or Backspace) back out; Home goes to the first part of the first chain. A visible focus ring uses the accent token (selection, by the colour rules). Works on the build Q74 lands (same focusable elements).
Definition of done:
1. On :8791 Tab reaches the diagram once and leaves it with the next Tab.
2. From a focused stock, Right moves focus to its outflow valve and again to the next stock, in Dynamics; in Blocks Right from a junction reaches C, then the actuator, then P.
3. Enter opens the panel with focus inside; Escape returns to the same part.
4. I on a system goes Into it and Escape returns with focus on that system.
5. The focus ring has at least 3:1 contrast in both themes.
Files: ergostat/web/static/interact.js, diagram.js, dynamics.js, blocks.js, style.css, tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
Acceptance tests: keyboard-only browser tests for 1-4 on :8791 in both views.
Budget: 160 net lines.

gaps.name: diagram-spoken-names
gaps.title: Every part of the diagram has a spoken name in its discipline's words, with its state and the loops it belongs to
gaps.definition:
Problem (R9 piece 5): the diagram is one unnamed SVG; a screen reader hears nothing useful for a stock, a valve, a connector or a block (shots/a11yb-8793-into-service-block-click.png, a11yb-8793-deadband-panel.png). Filed Q74 gives parts a name for focus; the names need to carry what a sighted reader sees.
Change: one function per view builds each part's accessible name (aria-label on the part's group, role img or button as Q74 set): Dynamics: 'stock users, 152 of desired 180, in product; in balancing loop word of mouth and 2 others'; 'flow signups, 3.1 per hour, from cloud to users'; 'connector from churn to support load, positive'; 'goal gap users-at-180, off by 28' (the goal's state is its `word` from the server when goal-row-one-renderer has landed, never a second mapping). Blocks: 'controller C keep-located-worked, on-off, control loop located-worked, off'; 'summing junction of located-worked: reference minus measurement'; 'signal e, error, minus 36'. System boxes: name, description, goals holding and off. Names use each discipline's words only (no 'sensor' in Dynamics), update with values on the poll without stealing focus, and the SVG itself has the caption of filed Q02 as its name.
Definition of done:
1. On :8791 in both views every focusable part has a non-empty aria-label containing its kind word and its name; none contains 'undefined' or a raw id with a colon.
2. A stock's label contains its value and unit; on a fixture an off goal's contains 'off'.
3. No Dynamics label contains 'sensor' or 'controller'; no Blocks label contains 'stock'.
4. A unit test covers the name function for each part kind in each view.
Files: ergostat/web/static/dynamics.js, blocks.js, process.js, diagram.js, tests (a JS unit test or a browser test reading labels).
Acceptance tests: the label sweep over the six demos; the vocabulary check in 3.
Budget: 120 net lines.

gaps.name: keyboard-story-in-browser-tests
gaps.title: A keyboard-only run of story H5 is part of the browser tests
gaps.definition:
Problem (R9 piece 6): story H5 (find the goal that is off and read why, without a mouse) failed in the review (shots/story-7-h5-loops-kbd.png), and no test would notice if it failed again after the keyboard work lands.
Change: add tests/test_keyboard_story.py (Playwright, keyboard events only, no mouse or page.click): on a seeded fixture with a planted off goal (not a live demo), from page load: Tab to the diagram; arrow to the system holding the off goal; I to go Into it; arrow to the off goal's gap; Enter to open its evidence; read the panel's first line through the accessibility tree; Escape back; then Tab to the nav and reach the Goals page and its first row's link. The test asserts focus is always visible (document.activeElement has a non-zero box on screen), that each step's accessible name matches the expected kind, and that the whole run takes fewer than 40 key presses. The same run is repeated in Blocks.
Definition of done:
1. The test passes on main once the keyboard gaps (filed Q74, Q75 and diagram-roving-focus-and-arrow-keys) are in, and fails if any of them regresses.
2. It runs with the other browser tests and is skipped under the same condition as tests/test_diagram_rendering.py.
3. The key-press budget is asserted.
Files: tests/test_keyboard_story.py.
Acceptance tests: the test itself.
Budget: 90 lines of test, 0 product code.

gaps.name: export-model-and-loops-markdown
gaps.title: Export the model behind the picture: Dynamics as a variable table and loop list, Blocks as a loop table, in Markdown
gaps.definition:
Problem (R10): WHY.md leads with design documents, proposals and projection, but Export offers SVG, Design SVG and PNG only (ergostat/web/static/export.js, 114 lines; shots/story-6-g8-export-menu.png, sdx-8796-export.png). An SD modeller cannot audit the equations in one pass; a control engineer cannot read the loops as a table. Story G8: picture yes, model no.
Change: two entries in the existing Export menu, each for the system drawn (what is open or entered), produced by a server endpoint so the CLI can use it too (GET /api/export?view=dynamics|blocks&format=md&system=...): (1) Dynamics 'Model (Markdown)': a variable table (name, kind: stock/flow/auxiliary/goal, unit, equation or sensor in words, value now), the flows per stock (in, out), and the loop list (name, R/B or '?', path, the goal it closes); (2) Blocks 'Loops (Markdown)': one row per control loop (goal, reference, measured output, controller and its law in words, actuator, process and whether identified, sensor and period, the goal's word). The document starts with the model's name, purpose, the moment and the window, and names the system. Equations use the same words as the panels (equations.js / block_fn). Download with a file name carrying project, view and date.
Definition of done:
1. On :8796 ?system=product Export > Model (Markdown) downloads a file whose variable table has one row per part drawn and whose loop list equals the side list's.
2. On :8791 ?view=blocks Export > Loops (Markdown) has one row per goal in view, with the law's words equal to the Blocks panel's.
3. The Markdown renders as tables (a test parses it).
4. The export of a snapshot file works offline or says it cannot.
Files: new ergostat/web/export_api.py, ergostat/web/server.py, ergostat/web/static/export.js, tests/test_export.py.
Acceptance tests: unit tests of both documents on a small spec; a browser test of the two menu entries.
Budget: 180 net lines.

gaps.name: export-dynamics-xmile
gaps.title: Export the Dynamics model as XMILE
gaps.definition:
Problem (R10 piece 4): an SD modeller cannot take the model to Stella or Vensim; both experts in the review called export of the model the biggest missed chance for their audience (shots/sdx-8796-model.png). XMILE is the OASIS interchange standard for system dynamics models.
Change: GET /api/export?view=dynamics&format=xmile&system=... and an Export menu entry 'Model (XMILE)'. A new ergostat/xmile.py (standard library only: xml.etree.ElementTree; no new runtime dependency) maps the spec's system dynamics view to XMILE 1.0: stocks with their inflows and outflows and initial value (the value at the window's start), flows with their fitted or declared equation when one exists (otherwise a graphical/table function of time from the recorded series, said in the documentation element), auxiliaries and goals (desired level and gap as auxiliaries), units, systems as modules (or as groups when the proposal on bundles has not landed), and sim_specs from the header's window. Parts ergostat cannot express (sensors, blocks, agents) are left out and listed in a comment header. Names are made XMILE-safe with the original in the doc element. No simulator is required by the tests: checking that another tool reproduces ergostat's replay is left out (it would need a third-party XMILE simulator in the test environment; a later gap may add it as an optional check if the owner wants it).
Definition of done:
1. The export of software-factory's product is well-formed XML with the XMILE 1.0 namespace and the required header, sim_specs and model elements (checked with the standard library in every run).
2. Schema validation: the OASIS XMILE v1.0 schema file (xmile.xsd, from the OASIS XMILE 1.0 specification's schemas, vendored under tests/fixtures/xmile/ with its licence note) validates the export; this one test uses the `xmlschema` package as an optional test dependency (declared in the dev group) and is skipped with a stated reason when it is not installed.
3. Every stock, flow and auxiliary drawn is present with its unit; every stock's inflows and outflows match the diagram's pipes.
4. A round check: a small spec with declared equations exports equations equal to the spec's (compared as text after XMILE's name rules).
Files: new ergostat/xmile.py, ergostat/web/export_api.py or server.py, ergostat/web/static/export.js, tests/test_xmile.py, tests/fixtures/xmile/xmile.xsd, pyproject.toml (dev group only).
Acceptance tests: the structure test, the schema validation (skippable), the pipes check, the equation round check.
Budget: 200 net lines.

gaps.name: export-loops-json-and-traces-csv
gaps.title: Export Blocks' loops as JSON and their traces as CSV
gaps.definition:
Problem (R10 piece 5): a control engineer cannot take P(s), C(z) and the traces to another tool (MATLAB, python-control); the identified models and the r/y/u/e series exist behind /api/loop-control and /api/loop-scope but only as drawings (shots/story-6-g8-export-blocks-*.png, ce-tf-export.png).
Change: two Export menu entries in Blocks, for the control loops in view: 'Loops (JSON)': per loop its goal, reference, sample period, the controller's law (type and parameters, as block_fn gives them), the identified process when there is one (numerator, denominator, delay, sample time, fit on held-out data) or 'not identified', sensor period, status; a documented, versioned shape. 'Traces (CSV)': one file per loop or one long-format file (time ISO 8601 with zone, loop, signal r/y/u/e/d, value) over the header's window at the scope's resolution. Served by GET /api/export?view=blocks&format=json|csv, built from the same functions as loop-control and loop-scope, with the identification taken from the cache and never recomputed per request.
Definition of done:
1. On :8791 ?view=blocks 'Loops (JSON)' has one entry per goal in view and validates against the documented shape (a JSON schema in docs or tests).
2. 'Traces (CSV)' for one loop has the same points as /api/loop-scope for the same window.
3. A loop with no identified process says so and still exports its law and traces.
4. The export does not trigger an identification (asserted by a counter).
Files: ergostat/web/export_api.py or server.py, ergostat/web/control_api.py (reuse), ergostat/web/static/export.js, tests/test_export.py, docs/SPEC.md (the shape).
Acceptance tests: unit tests for 1-4 on a small spec.
Budget: 90 net lines.

gaps.name: check-is-a-section-of-model
gaps.title: Check becomes a section of the Model page; the Check page and its nav entry go
gaps.definition:
Problem (R12 piece 1): eight top-level pages do not fit a phone or 200% zoom (shots/a11y-8792-zoom200-diagram.png, story-7-h4-phone-light.png), and with the owner's Dashboard the count grows. Check is a lint list for whoever maintains the model (pm-tf-check.png) and belongs with the Model page; filed Q78 already makes the two say each thing once in a table.
Change: the Check findings are a section 'Check' of the Model page (ergostat/web/static/review.js), as the table Q78 defines (finding, part, file:line as a link, what to do), folded when there are none ('Check: nothing found'). /check redirects to /model#check keeping its query (as /fit goes to /model, util.js:508-510); 'check' leaves the nav (index.html) and stays in UI_PAGES only as the redirect; links to Check elsewhere (attention entries, the header's attention level) point to /model#check. /api/check and `ergostat check` are unchanged. The net effect with the Dashboard is no growth in nav entries.
Definition of done:
1. The nav has no Check entry; /check lands on /model#check with the section open and scrolled to.
2. The section lists the same findings as /api/check.
3. No link on any page points to a dead /check.
4. At 390 px and at 200% zoom the nav fits on :8792 (with filed Q05).
5. docs (QUICKSTART, DESIGN, SPEC page list) updated.
Files: ergostat/web/static/index.html, util.js, review.js, pages.js (remove the Check page), diagram.js and state-derived links, docs/QUICKSTART.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/SPEC.md, tests/test_page_polling.py, tests/test_graph_cli_web.py.
Acceptance tests: the redirect test; the section-equals-API test; the nav test at 390 px.
Budget: 30 net lines (net of the removed page).

gaps.name: demo-loop-with-identified-process
gaps.title: A demo has a control loop with an identified process, so margins, step response and tuning appear
gaps.definition:
Problem (R12 piece 3): no loop in six demos has an identified process, so the controller panel says 'Its process is not identified yet, so no margins…' everywhere (shots/ceb-is-ctrl-panel.png) and the closed-loop step, Bode plot, margins and tuning advice that WHY.md argues for never appear. The doubt 'is it useful at all' cannot be answered from the demos.
Change (demo work, outside the page): in one demo (image-squeeze's service, whose queue is acted on by a proportional or PI block, or a small new loop in software-factory) the simulated plant gets dynamics that identification can find (a first-order lag with delay between command and stock, with enough excitation: a varying reference or disturbance in the seed), the controller is a continuous law rather than on-off, and the demo runs long enough at start (or ships a seeded record) for ergostat/web/control_api.py's identification to pass its held-out fit. The demo's README states what the controller panel should then show (identified P, gain and phase margins, the closed-loop step, a tuning suggestion).
Definition of done:
1. After the demo's start (or with its seeded record) /api/loop-control for that goal returns an identified process with held-out fit above the page's threshold.
2. Its controller panel shows margins and the closed-loop step, and no 'not identified' sentence.
3. `ergostat check` passes on the demo; tests/test_demo_check.py passes.
4. The README names the loop and what to look at.
Files: demos/image-squeeze or demos/software-factory (model, simulator, seed, README.md), tests/test_demo_check.py; no page code.
Acceptance tests: a demo test (skipped unless demos are enabled) asserting 1.
Budget: 150 net lines in the demo.

gaps.name: demo-observed-external-controller
gaps.title: A demo has an observed external controller (an autoscaler), identified and judged
gaps.definition:
Problem (R12 piece 4): ergostat is meant to sit on top of existing control systems and join them 'as another controller' (intent.md; docs/proposals/external-systems.md), but no demo has an observed external controller, so the claim that it can model, identify and judge a vendor's control loop (a Kubernetes autoscaler) is never shown.
Change (demo work): add to a demo (big's api system or a small new demo beside the kube simulation) a simulated horizontal autoscaler that ergostat does not run: it reads a request rate or utilisation, sets replicas with the autoscaler's usual rule (target utilisation, stabilisation window, scale-up/down limits), and emits only what a real cluster would expose (metrics and scaling events). The model declares it as an external block (the agents: entry `external: true`, an observed controller with its inputs and outputs), with stocks for replicas and load, the goal it serves, and sensors reading its metrics. ergostat identifies its law from the record, shows it in Blocks as a controller with its identified law and fit, and judges the loop (holding, oscillating, margins when the process is identified). The README says what to look at and what ergostat adds that the autoscaler's own dashboard does not.
Definition of done:
1. In the demo, Blocks draws the autoscaler as an external controller in its control loop with r (target), y (utilisation) and u (replicas).
2. /api/loop-control for its goal returns an identified law for the external controller with its fit, or says why not.
3. The Agents page lists it as external and not run by ergostat, with no runs of its own.
4. `ergostat check` passes; the demo's README has the walkthrough.
Files: demos/<demo> (model, simulator, README.md), tests/test_demo_check.py; no page code unless a defect is found (file it separately).
Acceptance tests: a demo test asserting 1-3.
Budget: 200 net lines in the demo.

gaps.name: goals-page-keep-or-fold-decision
gaps.title: Decision: once boxes carry goal rows and the Dashboard exists, does the Goals page stay?
gaps.owner_items: R1 piece 9, R12 piece 5 (the Agents half is already decided by the owner: Agents stays and gains a show page)
gaps.definition:
Problem (R1 piece 9, R12 piece 5): eight top-level pages do not fit a phone or 200% zoom (shots/a11y-8792-zoom200-diagram.png), and Goals, Agents and Model are tables of the same goals again. The owner has added two pages (Dashboard, Agent show) and renamed Loops to Goals. After the box rows and the Dashboard's goals panel are in use, the Goals page's rows exist in two other places, drawn by the same goalRow. With '/' kept as the folded diagram (decision 1), a newcomer must not get three competing first answers to 'is it healthy' (boxes, Goals, Dashboard). Whether the Goals page then goes is the owner's call, and it should be made on evidence, not in advance.
Change: a short decision record docs/proposals/goals-page.md: what the Goals page shows that the box rows and the Dashboard's goals panel do not (the sortable list of every goal, the performance column, filters in the address); three options with what each deletes: (a) keep it as the sortable list; (b) fold it into the Dashboard as its default (the Dashboard is still not the home page); (c) remove it, /goals redirecting to the diagram with the goal list in the side panel. For each: lines removed, links that must be redirected (filed Q17's headline link, the phone nav), and the story runs (B1, B3, H5, from the latest stories results) that still pass. One sentence for the owner. Then file the follow-up gap for the chosen option.
Definition of done:
1. The record exists with the three options measured against the story runs.
2. The owner's answer is recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.
3. The follow-up gap (if any) is requested with this gap as parent.
Files: docs/proposals/goals-page.md, docs/DECISIONS.md.
Acceptance tests: review only.
Budget: about 80 lines, no code.

gaps.name: stories-rerun-after-redesigns
gaps.title: The stories are walked again after the redesigns, and the count of possible-and-obvious stories is the plan's result
gaps.owner_items: All (R1-R12 measured by the review's own stories)
gaps.definition:
Problem: the twelve redesigns exist because 18 of 46 stories were impossible and none was possible and obvious. The plan's gaps each pass their own tests; whether the redesigns did what they were for is known only by walking the stories again, on the demos, after them. The earlier walk (stories-rerun-after-owner-list) covers the owner's list and R1's first pieces only.
Change: the same walk and the same record as stories-rerun-after-owner-list (every story of docs/roadmap/stories.md; steps, screenshot, verdict; the baseline and the earlier walk beside it), in docs/roadmap/stories-results/<date>.md, now including the Blocks stories (G5, G6, H1), the Dynamics stories (G3, G4), the forecast stories (B3, B4), the keyboard story (H5, cross-checked with tests/test_keyboard_story.py), the kind, agent and dashboard stories (F6, D5, B7) and the newcomer's vocabulary story A3 read against the Guide's frames. Each story that is still not 'possible and obvious' gets one requested gap naming the story, the failing step and the screenshot. The summary is sent to the owner in one sentence: how many of the stories are now possible and obvious, against 0 at the review.
Definition of done:
1. The results file has a row per story with all three verdicts side by side.
2. No story is 'not yet' for a surface whose gap has merged.
3. Every story not 'possible and obvious' has a requested gap.
4. The one-sentence summary is in the file's first line.
Files: docs/roadmap/stories-results/<date>.md, screenshots beside it.
Acceptance tests: review: every story has a row and every failure a requested gap.
Budget: documentation only.
